facts.fact: Mario Roberto Álvarez founded the firm MRA in 1947 with Leonardo Kopiloff and Eduardo T. Santoro, and its first major contract, in 1954, was the design of the municipal Teatro General San Martín, the largest centre for the stage in Argentina.
facts.quote: Joining colleagues Leonardo Kopiloff and Eduardo T. Santoro, he established MRA in 1947. The firm's first major contract would be in 1954 with their design for the municipal Teatro General San Martín, the largest center for the stage in Argentina.

facts.fact: The theatre was completed in 1960, and its success won MRA the design of the adjoining Centro Cultural General San Martín, built between 1962 and 1970.
facts.quote: Its success upon completion in 1960 helped secure MRA the design for the adjoining Centro Cultural General San Martín, built between 1962 and 1970.

facts.fact: The theatre and the cultural centre beside it stand on Corrientes Avenue in Buenos Aires.
facts.quote: Adjacent to the theatre of the same name inaugurated in 1970 on Corrientes Avenue, the cultural center was designed by local architect Mario Roberto Álvarez, and was built between 1962 and 1973.

facts.fact: Palacio Salvo is an eclectic skyscraper where 18 de Julio Avenue meets Plaza Independencia in central Montevideo.
facts.quote: The Palacio Salvo (English: Salvo Palace) is an eclectic skyscraper at the intersection of 18 de Julio Avenue and Plaza Independencia in the Centro neighbourhood of Montevideo, Uruguay.

facts.fact: It was briefly the tallest building in Latin America, and when finished it was the tallest reinforced concrete structure in the world.
facts.quote: It was the tallest building in Latin America for a brief period, at its completion it was the tallest reinforced concrete structure in the world.

facts.fact: It was designed by Mario Palanti, an Italian immigrant living in Buenos Aires, who used a similar design for his Palacio Barolo there.
facts.quote: It was designed by the architect Mario Palanti, an Italian immigrant living in Buenos Aires, who used a similar design for his Palacio Barolo in Buenos Aires, Argentina.

facts.fact: It has been a National Historical Monument of Uruguay since 1996.
facts.quote: Since 1996 it is a National Historical Monument of Uruguay.

facts.fact: It was first meant to be a hotel, but has instead been used for a mix of offices and private homes.
facts.quote: The building was originally intended to be a hotel, but this plan did not work out, and it has since been occupied by a mixture of offices and private residences.

facts.fact: Its eclectic style mixes Renaissance references, Gothic echoes and Neoclassical touches, and its silhouette has become an emblem of the city.
facts.quote: With an eclectic style that combines Renaissance references with Gothic reminiscences and Neoclassical touches, its distinctive silhouette has become an emblem of the city and a reminder of the prosperous years of the early 20th century.

facts.fact: Both the Salvo and the Barolo are inspired by Dante's Divine Comedy.
facts.quote: Both buildings are inspired by Dante Alighieri’s Divine Comedy, but only Palacio Barolo in Buenos Aires was designed with the intention of housing the author’s remains.

facts.fact: Palanti meant the lighthouses on the two domes to form a "bridge of light" across the Río de la Plata between the two cities.
facts.quote: The original idea of Italian immigrant Mario Palanti, the architect of both buildings, was to connect the two cities with a "bridge of light" over the Río de la Plata, using the lighthouses placed on their domes as a welcoming beacon to the region.

facts.fact: The Toba Sea-Folk Museum is devoted to the fishing traditions of the area around Toba, in Mie Prefecture, Japan.
facts.quote: Toba Sea-Folk Museum (鳥羽市立海の博物館, Toba Shiritsu Umi no Hakubutsukan) is a museum dedicated to the area's fishing traditions in Toba, Mie Prefecture, Japan.

facts.fact: The museum first opened privately in 1971, moved to its present site in 1992, and became a public municipal museum in 2017.
facts.quote: Having first opened as the private Sea-Folk Museum in 1971, the museum reopened in its current location in 1992, and in 2017 was reestablished as a public, municipal museum under its current name.

facts.fact: In 1998 the museum buildings, designed by Hiroshi Naito, were named among Japan's 100 Select Instances of Public Architecture by the Ministry of Construction.
facts.quote: In 1998, the museum buildings, designed by Naitō Hiroshi, were included amongst the 100 Select Instances of Public Architecture (公共建築百選) by the then Ministry of Construction.

facts.fact: The collection includes some ninety wooden boats from all over Japan and the country's most complete holdings on the Ama divers.
facts.quote: The collection, numbering some 61,840 items as of 31 March 2018, includes some ninety wooden boats from all over Japan, the nation's most comprehensive assemblage of materials relating to the Ama, and a grouping of 6,879 pieces of Ise Bay, Shima Peninsula, and Kumano Sea Fishing Equipment that have been jointly designated an Important Tangible Folk Cultural Property.

facts.fact: The displays are arranged around seven themes, from sea-folk faith and festivals to sea pollution and wooden boats.
facts.quote: The displays are organized around seven themes: traditions of sea-folk, sea-folk faith and festivals, sea pollution, Ama divers in Shima, fishing in Ise Bay, fishing in Shima and Kumano, and wooden boats and navigation.

facts.fact: The present City Hall was built in the late 1950s after a public campaign to give Hong Kong a civic centre again, on newly reclaimed seafront land.
facts.quote: The second and current City Hall complex was built in the late 1950s following a public campaign led by the Sino-British Club for the re-establishment of a civic centre in Hong Kong. It was built on a 10,000 square metres (110,000 sq ft) plot of land on the newly reclaimed seafront, about 200 metres (660 ft) from the first generation building.

facts.fact: Its foundation stone was laid on 25 February 1960 and it officially opened on 2 March 1962.
facts.quote: The foundation stone laying ceremony took place on 25 February 1960 with Sir Robert Brown Black, then Governor of Hong Kong, who also presided over the official opening ceremony on 2 March 1962.

facts.fact: Based on an original design by Professor Gordon Brown of Hong Kong University and his team, it was completed by British architects Ronald Phillips and Alan Fitch for HK$20 million.
facts.quote: The building complex erected at the present site based on the original design by Professor Gordon Brown, the first Head of Department of Architecture of Hong Kong University, together with his team including Patricia O'Reilly Mayne, was completed by British architects Ronald Phillips and Alan Fitch at the cost of HK$20 million.

facts.fact: With its clean lines and stark geometric forms, it is an example of the International Style.
facts.quote: With its clean lines and stark geometric forms, the new Hall is an example of the International style fashionable at the time.

facts.fact: It is built of steel and concrete, with much of its equipment in steel, glass and anodised aluminium.
facts.quote: The structure was constructed using steel and concrete, and much of the equipment was of steel, glass and anodised aluminium.

facts.fact: Its two separate blocks and gardens were laid out as one whole along a central axis.
facts.quote: The two separate blocks and gardens were laid out as a cohesive whole, along a central axis.

facts.fact: The large public Memorial Gardens and the piazza in front were meant to give "freedom of movement and a sense of unlimited space" in the busy city.
facts.quote: Thus, the out-sized public areas of the Memorial Gardens and the piazza in front were conceived as a natural extension to promote the "freedom of movement and a sense of unlimited space".

facts.fact: In 2022 it was declared a monument, the youngest and the first post-war building in Hong Kong to be so.
facts.quote: On 20 May 2022, the Hong Kong City Hall was declared a monument under the Antiquities and Monuments Ordinance. At the age of 60, it is the youngest as well as the first post-WW2 building in Hong Kong being declared as a monument.

facts.fact: Morpheus is a neo-futurist luxury hotel in Macau, run by Melco Resorts & Entertainment.
facts.quote: Morpheus is a neo-futurist luxury hotel in the Chinese special administrative region of Macau that is operated by Melco Resorts & Entertainment.

facts.fact: It opened in June 2018; TIME called it the world's first free-form exoskeleton-bound high-rise, a steel grid wrapping 40 storeys of glass, inspired by Chinese jade carving.
facts.quote: Opened in June 2018, TIME describes it as "the world's first free-form exoskeleton-bound high-rise: a grid of steel envelops 40 stories of glass with a fluidity inspired by  Chinese jade carving."

facts.fact: Designed by Zaha Hadid Architects, it was the first building in Asia without a single internal column, and it rises 153.7 m.
facts.quote: Designed by Zaha Hadid Architects and developed by Melco Resorts for USD $1.1 billion, the hotel is the first building in Asia without a singular internal column and tops out at 153.7 m (504 ft).

facts.fact: The architects faced a tight 6,850 square metre rectangular footprint and had to fit the new structure onto foundations already on the site.
facts.quote: Upon visiting the location, the firm found that it presented "an unusual set of challenges. First, the site offered a relatively tight 6,850 square metre (74,000 square foot) rectangular building footprint," and "the new superstructure had to be adjusted to fit a site already with foundations."

facts.fact: The design, inspired by Chinese jade artefacts, uses a twisting exoskeleton to support two towers and several skybridges.
facts.quote: The ultimate design was inspired by Chinese jade artifacts, with a twisting exoskeleton supporting two towers and multiple skybridges.

facts.fact: Construction began in 2014; the exoskeleton's steel plates were welded into unique shapes at a shipbuilding yard in Guangdong.
facts.quote: Construction on the building began in 2014. To fabricate the exoskeleton, structural steel plates were welded into unique shapes at a shipbuilding facility in Guangdong, "where workers were familiar with large, curved structures.

facts.fact: The exoskeleton's grid carries gravity and lateral loads, cutting the need for internal columns and leaving large open spaces inside.
facts.quote: The structural geometric grid of the exoskeleton takes on gravitational and lateral loads and reduces the need for internal columns, allowing for large open areas inside the hotel.

facts.fact: The hotel's 772 rooms include nine two-storey sky villas.
facts.quote: The hotel's 772 rooms include nine two-story "sky villas," three of which have private pools.

facts.fact: The Lanyang Museum is a museum about the local area, in Toucheng Township, Yilan County, Taiwan.
facts.quote: The Lanyang Museum (LYM; traditional Chinese: 蘭陽博物館; simplified Chinese: 兰阳博物馆; pinyin: Lányáng Bówùguǎn) is a museum about the local area in Toucheng Township, Yilan County, Taiwan.

facts.fact: The firm Artech won the design and construction of the museum in April 2000.
facts.quote: Artech architecture was awarded the design and construction for the museum in April 2000.

facts.fact: The museum opened to the public on 16 October 2010.
facts.quote: The museum was finally opened officially to public on 16 October 2010.

facts.fact: The design, by a team led by Kris Yao, was inspired by the cuestas, the tilted rock formations common along the Beiguan coast.
facts.quote: The museum building was designed by a team led by Kris Yao those design was inspired by the cuestas commonly seen along Beiguan Coast.

facts.fact: The roof rises from the ground at 20 degrees to meet a wall rising at 70 degrees, so the building emerges from the ground like the cuestas.
facts.quote: The museum adopts the geometric shapes of the cuestas where the roof protrudes from the ground at an angle of 20 degrees meeting a wall which rises from the ground at an angle of 70 degrees. Thus the building emerges from the ground in a similar fashion to those cuestas.

facts.fact: The exhibits show the landscape of Yilan: its mountains, plains and sea.
facts.quote: The museum features exhibits showcasing the topography of Yilan, including the mountains, the plains, and the sea.

facts.fact: In 2012 the museum won an International Architecture Award from the Chicago Athenaeum and the European Centre.
facts.quote: 2012 The Chicago Athenaeum Museum Of Architecture And Design, The European Centre of Architecture Art Design And Urban Studies:The International Architecture Award - Lanyang Museum

facts.fact: The Taipei Performing Arts Center is a performance centre in Shilin District, Taipei.
facts.quote: The Taipei Performing Arts Center (TPAC; traditional Chinese: 臺北表演藝術中心; simplified Chinese: 台北表演艺术中心; pinyin: Táiběi Biǎoyǎn Yìshù Zhōngxīn) is a performance center in Shilin District, Taipei, Taiwan.

facts.fact: OMA won the competition for the centre in January 2009, and it opened in 2022.
facts.quote: In January 2009 OMA won the competition to build the Taipei Performing Arts Center in Taiwan, completed and opened in 2022.

facts.fact: Construction began in 2012.
facts.quote: The construction of the center began in 2012.

facts.fact: After a trial opening in spring 2022, it officially opened on 2 July 2022.
facts.quote: The center had a trial opening in March–May 2022 before it officially opened on 2 July 2022.

facts.fact: It was designed by David Gianotten and Rem Koolhaas at OMA.
facts.quote: The center was designed by David Gianotten and Rem Koolhaas at Office for Metropolitan Architecture.

facts.fact: A cube-shaped structure sits at the centre, along with a sphere-shaped playhouse seating 800.
facts.quote: At the center, there is a cube-shaped structure. It also consists the sphere-shaped playhouse which has a capacity of 800 seats.

facts.fact: The Grand Theater is an asymmetrical volume seating 1,500.
facts.quote: The Grand Theater is an asymmetrical-shaped building which has a capacity of 1,500 seats.

facts.fact: The Blue Box, for experimental performances, seats 500.
facts.quote: The Blue Box for experimental performances has a capacity of 500 seats.

facts.fact: Leeum is a museum in Hannam-dong, Seoul, run by the Samsung Foundation of Culture.
facts.quote: The Leeum Museum of Art (Korean: 리움미술관) is a museum in Hannam-dong, Yongsan District, Seoul, South Korea. It is run by the Samsung Foundation of Culture.

facts.fact: It is considered one of South Korea's top three private art museums.
facts.quote: It is considered one of South Korea's top three private art museums.

facts.fact: The museum has two parts, one for traditional Korean art and one for contemporary art.
facts.quote: The museum consists of two parts, one of which houses traditional Korean art, the other contemporary art.

facts.fact: The first part was designed by Mario Botta, the second by Jean Nouvel and Rem Koolhaas.
facts.quote: The first part of the museum was designed by Swiss architect Mario Botta and the second part of the museum by French architect Jean Nouvel and Dutch architect Rem Koolhaas.

facts.fact: Mario Botta designed Museum One (M1) in 2004.
facts.quote: In 2004, he designed Museum One (M1) of the Leeum, Samsung Museum of Art in Seoul, South Korea.

facts.fact: Museum 2 shows modern and contemporary art by Korean and foreign artists, with permanent spaces for Damien Hirst, Andy Warhol, Mark Rothko, Yves Klein and Donald Judd.
facts.quote: Museum 2 (M2) houses modern and contemporary art from Korean and foreign artists including Damien Hirst, Andy Warhol, Mark Rothko, Yves Klein, and Donald Judd have permanent exhibition spaces.

facts.fact: The National Gallery Singapore is a public art museum holding more than 9,000 works of Singaporean and Southeast Asian art from the 19th century to today.
facts.quote: The National Gallery Singapore is a public art museum and national museum located in the Civic District of Singapore. It houses a collection of Singaporean and Southeast Asian art spanning the 19th century to the present, with more than 9,000 artworks.

facts.fact: It is made from two national monuments, the former Supreme Court and the former City Hall, and with 64,000 square metres of floor it is the largest museum in Singapore.
facts.quote: It consists of two national monuments, the former Supreme Court and former City Hall buildings, and has a combined floor area of 64,000 square metres (690,000 sq ft), making it the largest visual arts venue and largest museum in Singapore.

facts.fact: Because both buildings are national monuments, parts such as the façades and some historic rooms could not be changed, though roof and basement floors could be added.
facts.quote: Due to the status of the former Supreme Court Building and City Hall as national monuments, certain aspects of the buildings could not be altered, such as the façade, the Surrender Chamber, the office of Singapore's founding Prime Minister and the panelling in four rooms of the Supreme Court. However, this still left many design options open such as the addition of roof and basement floors.

facts.fact: In May 2008 Studio Milou, with CPG Consultants, was appointed to design and build the Gallery.
facts.quote: In May 2008, Studio Milou Singapore, in partnership with CPG Consultants (Singapore), was appointed to design and build the Gallery.

facts.fact: Studio Milou's design linked the two buildings at roof level with a draped canopy held up by tree-like columns.
facts.quote: Studio Milou Architecture's design consisted of a linear draped canopy supported by tree-like columns to link the former Supreme Court Building and City Hall at the roof level.

facts.fact: Construction began in January 2011 and the Gallery opened on 24 November 2015.
facts.quote: Construction began in January 2011, and the Gallery opened to the public on 24 November 2015.

facts.fact: The two buildings face the Padang and are joined by bridges and a new basement level.
facts.quote: The buildings face the Padang and are connected by bridges and a new basement level.

facts.fact: The project won Singapore's President's Design Award, Design of the Year, in 2015.
facts.quote: studioMilou Architecture, working with CPG Consultants, was appointed after an international competition and the completed project received Singapore's President's Design Award, Design of the Year in 2015.

facts.fact: The Pinnacle@Duxton is a 50-storey public housing development in central Singapore; its seven linked towers are together the world's tallest public residential buildings.
facts.quote: The Pinnacle@Duxton is a 50-storey residential development in Singapore's city centre, next to the business district. All seven connected towers are collectively the world's tallest public residential buildings, and featuring the two longest sky gardens ever built on skyscrapers, at 500m each.

facts.fact: Unusually for Housing and Development Board (HDB) projects, its design came from a worldwide competition with 227 entries from 32 countries.
facts.quote: Unique amongst Housing and Development Board (HDB) projects, it is the design winner of a worldwide competition which attracted 227 entries from 32 countries.

facts.fact: The competition was won by ARC Studio Architecture + Urbanism with RSP Architects Planners & Engineers.
facts.quote: It was eventually won by two Singapore architecture companies, ARC Studio Architecture + Urbanism, in collaboration with RSP Architects Planners & Engineers.

facts.fact: The towers are linked on the 26th and 50th floors by two sky gardens, each 500 m long.
facts.quote: All seven towers in the development are collectively the world's tallest public housing residential buildings. They are linked at the 26th and 50th floors by the world's two longest sky gardens of 500m each.

facts.fact: The sky gardens hold jogging tracks, playgrounds and places to rest and look out.
facts.quote: The sky gardens at both levels incorporate jogging tracks, with playgrounds, rest and viewing areas, features which are unique and pioneering for skyscrapers at that time.

facts.fact: Buyers could choose combinations of balconies, planter boxes and bay windows, and the light concrete inner walls can be removed and rearranged.
facts.quote: Buyers are able to choose their flat's layout from combinations of balconies, planter boxes and/or bay windows. Also, the internal lightweight concrete walls can be easily removed and reconfigured by owners.

facts.fact: It was built with fully pre-cast methods, hoisting moulded parts into place.
facts.quote: Fully pre-cast methods were used during construction, which could be 10–15 per cent more expensive than the traditional way of pumping wet concrete all the way to the top. Pre-cast methods involve transporting moulded components to the site and hoisting them up on to the structure.

facts.fact: It won the 2010 Best Tall Building (Asia and Australasia) award from the CTBUH and a 2011 Urban Land Institute Global Award for Excellence.
facts.quote: Pinnacle@Duxton was conferred the 2010 Best Tall Building (Asia and Australasia) award by the Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat, as well as the 2011 Urban Land Institute's Global Awards for Excellence.

facts.fact: The airport was officially opened on 27 June 1998, shortly before the 1998 Commonwealth Games.
facts.quote: Kuala Lumpur International Airport was officially inaugurated by the tenth Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Tuanku Ja'afar of Negeri Sembilan, on 27 June 1998, shortly before the 1998 Commonwealth Games.

facts.fact: Terminal 1 was designed by Japanese architect Kisho Kurokawa, with an emphasis on natural light.
facts.quote: Terminal 1 was designed by Japanese architect Kisho Kurokawa, who also designed the Domestic Terminal (T2) at Nursultan Nazarbayev International Airport, with an emphasis of natural lighting within the airport complex.

facts.fact: Kurokawa's architecture, laid out on a 38.4 m grid that allows expansion, combines Islamic geometry and modern technology with the tropical rainforest in mind.
facts.quote: Spanning 38.4m along a grid pattern allowing for future expansions, the abstract symbolic architecture by the late Kisho Kurokawa encompasses the Islamic geometry and cutting-edge technology with the tropical rainforest in mind.

facts.fact: The Main Terminal Building sits between the two runways.
facts.quote: The KLIA Main Terminal Building (MTB) now also referred to as KLIA Main is located in between the two runways.

facts.fact: The main terminal covers 390,000 m² and is made of 39 square roof units, so the building can be extended.
facts.quote: The floor area of the terminal covers 390,000 m2 (4,200,000 sq ft) and the building consists of 39 square roof units, which enables future expansion of the building.

facts.fact: The satellite terminal has a natural rainforest at its centre.
facts.quote: The terminal also features a natural rainforest in the middle of the terminal, exhibiting the Malaysian rainforests.

facts.fact: Kurokawa won the Dedalo-Minosse International Prize in 2003 for the airport, and KLIA received the UN's Green Globe 21 certification for environmental responsibility.
facts.quote: In 2003 he was awarded the Dedalo-Minosse International Prize (Grand Prix) for his creation of the Kuala Lumpur International Airport in Malaysia and KLIA is the first and only airport in the world to receive the United Nations' Green Globe 21 certification for the airport's commitment to environmental responsibility each year since 2004.

facts.fact: Sumet Jumsai designed the Robot Building for the Bank of Asia to reflect the computerisation of banking, as a reaction against neoclassical and high-tech postmodern architecture.
facts.quote: It was designed for the Bank of Asia by Sumet Jumsai to reflect the computerization of banking; its architecture is a reaction against neoclassical and high-tech postmodern architecture.

facts.fact: Sumet found inspiration in his son's toy robot.
facts.quote: He had been asked by the Bank of Asia's directors to design a building that reflected the modernization and computerization of banking and found inspiration in his son's toy robot.

facts.fact: He called his design post-high-tech: instead of showing the building's workings, it dresses a finished building in abstracted machine parts.
facts.quote: He wrote that his design might be considered post-high-tech: rather than exhibiting the building's inner workings, he chose to adorn a finished product with the abstractions of mechanical parts.

facts.fact: It was completed in 1986 for US$10 million.
facts.quote: The building was completed in 1986 at a cost of US$10 million.

facts.fact: The floors step back at several levels, which gives the robot look and also meets setback rules requiring an 18-degree incline from the property line.
facts.quote: The floor areas decrease progressively at the 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th, and 18th floors; the staggered shape both contributes to the robot's appearance and is an efficient solution to setback regulations requiring an 18 degree incline from each side of the property line.

facts.fact: The two roof antennas serve for communications and as lightning rods.
facts.quote: Two antennas on the building's roof are used for communications and as lightning rods.

facts.fact: The robot's 6 m eyes are windows of reflective glass with metal louvre lids.
facts.quote: On the building's upper facade, in front of the main meeting and dining rooms of the top executive suites, are two 6 m (20 ft) lidded eyeballs that serve as windows. The eyeballs are made of reflective glass; the lids are made of metallic louvers.

facts.fact: The Museum of Contemporary Art, Los Angeles, chose it as one of the 50 seminal buildings of the century.
facts.quote: The Robot Building was selected by the Museum of Contemporary Art, Los Angeles as one of the 50 seminal buildings of the century.

facts.fact: The Sirius Building was designed in 1978–1979 by Housing Commission architect Tao Gofers and is a prominent example of Brutalism in Australia.
facts.quote: Designed for the Housing Commission of New South Wales in 1978–1979 by commission architect Tao Gofers, the building is a prominent example of Brutalist architecture in Australia.

facts.fact: Its repetitive geometries respond to Japanese Metabolism.
facts.quote: It also has striking repetitive geometries in reaction to the Japanese metabolist architecture movement.

facts.fact: Sirius had 79 apartments of one to four bedrooms, from single-storey flats to two- and three-storey walk-ups.
facts.quote: Notable for being the only high rise development in The Rocks, Sirius housed 79 apartments with one, two, three or four bedrooms, generally with single storey apartments to two and three storey walk ups.

facts.fact: It was built to rehouse public tenants displaced by the controversial redevelopment of The Rocks in the 1960s and 70s.
facts.quote: The complex was built to rehouse public tenants who had been displaced after a controversial redevelopment of the historic Rocks suburb during the 1960s and 70s.

facts.fact: Gofers meant the building to be white, to match the nearby Opera House, but budget limits left it unpainted.
facts.quote: Like that development, Gofers’ original plan was to finish the building in a white colour to match the nearby Sydney Opera House, but due to budget constraints, the building was finished unpainted.

facts.fact: The NSW government refused heritage listing in 2017 against the Heritage Council's advice, and the building was put up for sale.
facts.quote: Following the NSW Government's decision to refuse heritage listing in 2017, against the advice of the Heritage Council of New South Wales, the building was put up for sale.

facts.fact: It was on the World Monuments Fund's 2018 list of monuments at risk.
facts.quote: The Sirius building is included on the World Monuments Fund's 2018 list of monuments at risk, with the listing calling "on the government of New South Wales to respect the recommendation of its heritage experts and allow its citizens to maintain an important social legacy".

facts.fact: In 2018 it won the Enduring Architecture Award from the NSW Australian Institute of Architects.
facts.quote: In 2018, the building won the Enduring Architecture Award from NSW Australian Institute of Architects.

facts.fact: One Central Park is a mixed-use twin tower in Chippendale, Sydney, built as the first stage of the Central Park renewal project.
facts.quote: One Central Park is a mixed-use dual skyscraper located in the Sydney suburb of Chippendale in New South Wales, Australia. Developed as a joint venture between Frasers Property and Sekisui House, it was constructed by Besix Watpac as the first stage of the Central Park urban renewal project.

facts.fact: The Central Park site was formerly occupied by Carlton & United Breweries.
facts.quote: Formerly occupied by Carlton & United Breweries, the site of Central Park was purchased by Frasers Property for $208 million in 2007.

facts.fact: Ateliers Jean Nouvel and PTW Architects together formed the architectural team.
facts.quote: Whilst Ateliers Jean Nouvel and PTW Architects worked in collaboration to form the basis of the One Central Park architectural team, two interior architects were separately utilised for the east and west towers.

facts.fact: The building opened officially in December 2013.
facts.quote: The official opening of One Central Park occurred later that year, in December 2013.

facts.fact: Its vertical gardens came from a collaboration between botanist Patrick Blanc and Ateliers Jean Nouvel, and rising over 50 metres they became the world's tallest vertical garden.
facts.quote: One Central Park's vertical gardens were inspired by the collaboration of French botanist Patrick Blanc and the architects Ateliers Jean Nouvel with LED art by Yann Kersalé. A living tapestry of plants, flowers and vines which stretch over 50 metres high, it has become the world's tallest vertical garden.

facts.fact: A heliostat cantilevered from the 28th floor of the east tower reflects daylight down into the gardens and atrium.
facts.quote: Suspended from the 28th floor of One Central Park's east tower, it serves not only as a predominant design element to the building but as a way of reflecting light to the gardens and atrium below.

facts.fact: Motorised mirrors on the west tower's roof track the sun and reflect light up to the cantilever.
facts.quote: It operates through a series of motorised mirrors that are positioned 100 metres below the cantilever on the rooftop of the west tower. Daylight is automatically tracked from these mirrors and the light is reflected up to the cantilever.

facts.fact: It won the CTBUH's Best Tall Building Worldwide award.
facts.quote: Winner of the Best Tall Building Worldwide from the Council for Tall Building and Urban Habitat (global).

facts.fact: The granite-clad station building was designed by Eliel Saarinen and opened in 1919.
facts.quote: The station building, clad in granite, was designed by Eliel Saarinen and inaugurated in 1919.

facts.fact: It is known for its clock tower and Emil Wikström's Lantern Bearers statues.
facts.quote: The building is known for its clock tower and the Lyhdynkantajat ("The Lantern Bearers") statues by Emil Wikström.

facts.fact: Saarinen won the design competition with a National Romantic entry, with sturdy walls, bears and towers.
facts.quote: The contest was won by Eliel Saarinen's entry Bevingadt hjul på en jordglob – Maapallolla seisova siipipyörä ("A winged wheel standing on a globe"), with a pure national romanticist design, with sturdy walls, eight bears, one tall sharp-pointed tower and numerous smaller towers, as well as a beautifully drawn stone portal to the main platform.

facts.fact: The design set off a debate about the architecture of public buildings, with calls for a modern, rational style.
facts.quote: The design sparked off a vigorous debate about the architecture of major public buildings, with demands for a modern, rational style.

facts.fact: After returning to Finland in 1904, Saarinen dropped romanticism and redesigned the station with a more rational design.
facts.quote: After coming back home to Finland in 1904 he abandoned romanticism altogether and re-designed the station completely, with a more rational design.

facts.fact: The halls have monumental reinforced-concrete vaults, then the largest such structure commissioned by the Finnish state.
facts.quote: The halls received monumental concrete vaults, clearly reflecting into the shape of the building. These vaults, utilising the Hennebique iron-reinforced concrete structure patented in France in 1892, were the largest iron-reinforced concrete structure commissioned by the state at the time.

facts.fact: The main facade and the statues at the entrance are of red granite from Hanko.
facts.quote: The main facade and the stone statues at the main entrance were made of red granite brought from Hanko.

facts.fact: The BBC named it one of the world's most beautiful railway stations in 2013.
facts.quote: Helsinki Central was chosen as one of the world's most beautiful railway stations by BBC in 2013.

facts.fact: The Slovak Radio Building is shaped like an upside-down pyramid; locals call it the Radio Diamant.
facts.quote: It is shaped like an upside down pyramid. Locals also refer to it as the Radio Diamant.

facts.fact: Its architects were Štefan Svetko, Štefan Ďurkovič and Barnabáš Kissling; it was begun in 1967 and completed in 1983.
facts.quote: Architects of this project were Štefan Svetko, Štefan Ďurkovič and Barnabáš Kissling and it was completed in 1983. The project began in 1967.

facts.fact: The building is 80 metres high and has a 522-seat concert hall with a large organ.
facts.quote: The building is 80 metres high and has a 522-seat concert hall with a large concert organ.

facts.fact: The architects came second in a 1963 competition, but the client chose their design over the winning one by Miloš Chorvát.
facts.quote: Although the competition was won by Miloš Chorvát, the investor opted for the second-placed design by Štefan Svetko, Štefan Ďurkovič and Barnabáš Kissling.

facts.fact: The architects deliberately avoided the usual low block with a tall office tower, aiming for a more expressive building.
facts.quote: The authors consciously sought to avoid replicating the predominant style of tall buildings at the time, which combined a low block with a tall office tower. The building was instead meant to be more expressive and carry a distinctive style.

facts.fact: It was one of the first major buildings in Slovakia with a steel frame instead of the usual prefabricated concrete panels.
facts.quote: The Slovak Radio Building was one of the first major buildings in Slovakia utilizing a steel frame instead of prefabricated concrete panels which were ubiquitous at the time.

facts.fact: Svetko called the design a "temple of word and music".
facts.quote: Štefan Svetko was known to refer to the design as a "temple of word and music".

facts.fact: In 2017 it was declared a cultural heritage monument of Slovakia.
facts.quote: In 2017, the building was declared a cultural heritage monument in Slovakia.

facts.fact: The cemetery was built in 1965 to honour the Yugoslav Partisans of Mostar killed in the Second World War.
facts.quote: It was built in 1965 in honor of the Yugoslav Partisans of Mostar who were killed during World War II in Yugoslavia.

facts.fact: It lies at Bijeli Brijeg, on the slopes of Hum hill on the right bank of the Neretva.
facts.quote: The Partisan Memorial Cemetery in Mostar is constructed on the locality called Bijeli Brijeg, on the slopes of Hum hill on the right bank of the Neretva river, in Mostar.

facts.fact: At Džemal Bijedić's initiative, the Belgrade architect Bogdan Bogdanović was put in charge of the design.
facts.quote: At the initiative of Džemal Bijedić, the Belgrade architect Bogdan Bogdanović was put in charge of the design.

facts.fact: Civil engineer Ahmet Ribica led the drilling and blasting of the hillside and the building of the monument.
facts.quote: Ahmet Ribica, a civil engineer, was in charge of drilling and dynamiting works on the hill and constructing the monument.

facts.fact: Josip Broz Tito opened it on 25 September 1965, the 20th anniversary of Mostar's liberation.
facts.quote: On 25 September 1965, the 20th anniversary of the liberation of Mostar and the formation of the Mostar Battalion, it was opened by Josip Broz Tito.

facts.fact: It was badly damaged by war and blasting in 1992.
facts.quote: In 1992, the cemetery was badly damaged by war and dynamiting.

facts.fact: In 2006 it was proclaimed a national monument of Bosnia and Herzegovina.
facts.quote: In 2006, the cemetery was proclaimed a national monument of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

facts.fact: The campus was designed by Achyut Kanvinde, planned and landscaped for environmental freedom and ease of movement and communication.
facts.quote: The campus, which is planned and landscaped with the goal of environmental freedom, ease of movement and communication, was designed by Achyut Kanvinde.

facts.fact: The institute moved to its present site near Kalyanpur in 1963.
facts.quote: In 1963, the institute moved to its present location, on the Grand Trunk Road near Kalyanpur locality in Kanpur district.

facts.fact: The academic area holds the central library, department buildings, research centres, lecture hall complex, tutorial block and auditorium.
facts.quote: The academic area comprises the central library, departmental buildings, research centres, lecture hall complex, tutorial block and auditorium.

facts.fact: Student hostels, the Student Activities Centre and sports facilities lie outside the academic area.
facts.quote: The student hostels and other facilities like Student Activities Centre (SAC), Sports Complex lie outside the academic area.

facts.fact: The campus covers 4.3 square kilometres.
facts.quote: The campus is spread over an area of 4.3 square kilometres (1,100 acres).

facts.fact: The museum holds Gandharan sculpture, ancient and medieval Indian sculpture and Pahari and Rajasthani miniatures.
facts.quote: Government Museum and Art Gallery, Chandigarh, is a public museum of North India having collections of Gandharan sculptures, sculptures from ancient and medieval India, Pahari and Rajasthani miniature paintings.

facts.fact: It was built to house the art received from the Lahore Museum at the partition of India.
facts.quote: The Government Museum and Art Gallery were built for housing the artefacts received from the Lahore Museum during the partition of India.

facts.fact: Le Corbusier designed it with Pierre Jeanneret, Manmohan Nath Sharma and Shiv Dutt Sharma; the design dates from 1960–62 and it was built between 1962 and 1967.
facts.quote: The building was designed by the Swiss-born French architect, Le Corbusier along with his associate architects namely Manmohan Nath Sharma, Pierre Jeanneret and Shiv Dutt Sharma. The design was completed during 1960-62 and construction took place between 1962 and 1967.

facts.fact: It is one of three museums by Le Corbusier, with the Sanskar Kendra in Ahmedabad and the National Museum of Western Art in Tokyo.
facts.quote: It is one of the three museums designed by Le Corbusier, the other two being Sanskar Kendra, in Ahmedabad, and National Museum of Western Art, in Tokyo.

facts.fact: The museum opened on 6 May 1968.
facts.quote: The museum was inaugurated on 6 May 1968 by Dr. M. S. Randhawa, the then Chief Commissioner of Chandigarh.

facts.fact: Its pivoting entrance, metal-panelled door, fixed furniture, display systems and exposed concrete gargoyles are typical of Chandigarh's architecture.
facts.quote: The pivoted entrance, metal-panelled door, fixed furniture, display systems, and exposed concrete sculpturesque gargoyles are symbolic of the prevailing style of Chandigarh's architecture.

facts.fact: A mural by Satish Gujral in the reception adds colour to the otherwise stark exposed concrete building.
facts.quote: The mural in the museum reception area executed by one of India's finest contemporary artists, Satish Gujral adds colour to the otherwise stark exposed concrete building.

facts.fact: Its second level holds the main galleries: Gandhara sculpture, Indian miniatures, stone and metal sculpture, coins and contemporary Indian art.
facts.quote: Level 2 is 23,000 sq ft and comprises exhibition space for sections on Gandhara sculpture, Indian miniature paintings, stone and metal sculpture, coins and Indian contemporary art.

facts.fact: The Rock Garden is a sculpture garden in Chandigarh, begun in secret in 1957 by Nek Chand, a government official, in his spare time.
facts.quote: It is also known as Nek Chand Saini's Rock Garden of Nathupur  after its founder Nek Chand Saini, a government official who started building the garden secretly in his spare time in 1957.

facts.fact: It covers 40 acres and is built entirely from industrial and household waste and discarded objects.
facts.quote: It has spread over an area of 40 acres (16 ha), and is completely built from industrial, home waste, and discarded items.

facts.fact: Nek Chand gathered materials from demolition sites around the city and built in a forest gorge near Sukhna Lake.
facts.quote: In his spare time, Nek Chand started collecting materials from demolition sites around the city. He recycled these materials into his own vision of the divine kingdom of Sukrani, choosing a gorge in a forest near Sukhna Lake for his work.

facts.fact: Chand hid the illegal work for 18 years until the authorities found it in 1975.
facts.quote: Chand's work was illegal, but he was able to hide it for 18 years before it was discovered by the authorities in 1975.

facts.fact: By then it had become a complex of linked courtyards filled with pottery-covered concrete sculptures of dancers, musicians and animals.
facts.quote: By this time, it had grown into a 12-acre (4.9 ha) complex of interlinked courtyards, each filled with hundreds of pottery-covered concrete sculptures of dancers, musicians, and animals.

facts.fact: Chand built up each form with cement and sand, then coated it in burnished cement set with broken glass, bangles, crockery, mosaic and foundry slag.
facts.quote: Chand built up the mass with a cement and sand mix made from recycled materials before adding a final coating of smoothly burnished pure cement combined with waste materials such as broken glass, bangles, crockery, mosaic, and iron-foundry slag.

facts.fact: Public opinion saved it from demolition, and in 1986 it was inaugurated as a public space.
facts.quote: His work was in serious danger of being demolished, but he was able to get public opinion on his side, and in 1986 the park was inaugurated as a public space.

facts.fact: The garden is valued as a pioneer of environmental art and recycling.
facts.quote: The Rock Garden is acclaimed for its pioneering role in the environmental art and recycling movement.

facts.fact: Mazar-e-Quaid is the tomb of Muhammad Ali Jinnah, the founder of Pakistan.
facts.quote: Mazar-e-Quaid (Urdu: مزارِ قائد, lit. 'Tomb of the Leader'), also known as Jinnah Mausoleum or the National Mausoleum, is the final resting place of Muhammad Ali Jinnah, the founder of Pakistan.

facts.fact: Fatima Jinnah blocked the 1957 competition design and commissioned Yahya Merchant, a Bombay architect and friend of Jinnah.
facts.quote: Fatima Jinnah effectively vetoed the 1957 proposal, and assumed control of the QMF. She then commissioned architect Yahya Merchant, a Bombay based architect who was a personal friend of Jinnah, to design the monument.

facts.fact: The foundation stone was laid on 31 July 1960 and the mausoleum was inaugurated on 18 January 1971.
facts.quote: President Ayub Khan laid the foundation stone for the monument on 31 July 1960. It was inaugurated by Yahya Khan on 18 January 1971.

facts.fact: Merchant's design is a domed cube clad in white marble, on a raised platform in a 61-acre garden on a hill.
facts.quote: Merchant's design was of a cuboid structure with a dome, clad in white marble. The monument was placed on an elevated platform, set in a 61-acre gardened hill looking over the city.

facts.fact: It is a traditional design with a light modernist influence, called a "traditional monument of a modernist period".
facts.quote: The mausoleum was designed in a traditional style with a minor influence of modernist style popular during the 1960s and 1970s, and has been termed a "traditional monument of a modernist period."

facts.fact: White marble and pure geometric forms were chosen to suggest purity and to present Jinnah as larger than life.
facts.quote: The use of white marble to suggest purity, and pure geometric forms, are designed to portray Jinnah as a larger-than-life figure.

facts.fact: It has curved arches and copper grilles, and a four-tier crystal chandelier given by China hangs in the inner sanctum.
facts.quote: It is clad in white marble, and has curved arches and copper grills set on an elevated 54-square-metre platform.  The cool inner sanctum reflects the green of a four-tiered crystal chandelier given by the People's Republic of China.

facts.fact: The building is 75 by 75 m and 43 m high, on a 4 m platform, with an entrance in each wall.
facts.quote: The mausoleum is located in a 53-hectare park and the building has a footprint of 75 by 75 m (246 by 246 ft) with a height of 43 m (141 ft), built on a 4 m (13 ft) high platform. In each wall is placed an entrance.

facts.fact: The Patan Museum opened in 1997 and lies within a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
facts.quote: The museum falls under the UNESCO's World Heritage Sites. The Patan Museum was inaugurated in 1997 by Late King Birendra Bir Bikram Shah.

facts.fact: It is housed in an old residential court of Patan Durbar, a royal palace of the Malla kings.
facts.quote: Its home is an old residential court of Patan Durbar, one of the royal palaces of former Malla Kings of the Kathmandu Valley.

facts.fact: The building was restored by Austrian architect Götz Hagmüller.
facts.quote: The Museum was restored by the Austrian architect the late Götz Hagmüller and the collection of the Museum itself was curated by the Late Mary Shepherd Slusser.

facts.fact: The palace was built on the site of a Buddhist monastery and has been renovated many times.
facts.quote: The royal palace was built on the site of a Buddhist monastery. It has been renovated many times.

facts.fact: The east wing was destroyed in the 1934 earthquake and rebuilt.
facts.quote: In the 1934 earthquake the east wing was destroyed and later rebuilt.

facts.fact: In 2017 the restored Sundari Chowk courtyard was added to the museum, with a traditional mud floor.
facts.quote: In 2017 the restored palace courtyard Sundari Chowk was added to the museum, creating room for the new Seamann Gallery and the Frozen Wall. Unlike the tiled floors in the rest of the museum, the floor here is covered with mud, the traditional Nepalese floor covering.

facts.fact: The collection is mostly cast bronzes and gilt copper repoussé work, crafts Patan is famous for.
facts.quote: Most of the objects are cast bronzes (mostly sculptures of Hindu and Buddhist deities) and gilt copper repoussé work, crafts for which Patan is famous.

facts.fact: Designed by Skidmore, Owings & Merrill, the hotel opened in 1955 and is the longest-running Hilton outside the United States.
facts.quote: Designed by Skidmore, Owings & Merrill, it opened in 1955 as the Istanbul Hilton and is the longest operating Hilton Hotel outside the United States.

facts.fact: Turkish architect Sedad Hakkı Eldem was appointed as an adviser, and the design was a collaboration between Eldem and Gordon Bunshaft.
facts.quote: Turkish architect Sedat Hakkı Eldem was appointed as an advisor. The design of the Istanbul Hilton was a joint collaboration by Sedat Hakkı Eldem (Turkish architect) and Gordon Bunshaft.

facts.fact: The Hilton project became part of the Cold War rivalry between the US and the Soviet Union.
facts.quote: The Istanbul Hilton project thus became a factor in the Cold War US–Soviet rivalry.

facts.fact: The eleven-storey building is a rectangular slab 21 m by 100 m, set on a green hillside with a panoramic view of the Bosphorus.
facts.quote: The eleven-story building, in the form of a rectangular prism with dimensions of 21 m × 100 m (69 ft × 328 ft), represents modern architecture. The building was erected on a green hillside with a panoramic view of the Bosphorus and is very close to the busy Taksim Square.

facts.fact: It combines Bunshaft's modern lines with Ottoman and Turkish artistic elements added by Eldem.
facts.quote: The building is a combination of the modern lines of Gordon Bunshaft with the rich artistic and romantic elements of Ottoman and Turkish architecture, implemented by its architect, Sedat Hakkı Eldem.

facts.fact: Eldem's roof over the main entrance resembles a flying carpet.
facts.quote: As an example of Orientalism, the roof of the main entrance, designed by Eldem, resembles a flying carpet.

facts.fact: Materials came from abroad: white cement, glass and steel from Germany, marble and ceramics from Italy, and aluminium window castings from the US.
facts.quote: White Portland cement, glass and structural steel came from Germany, marble and ceramic fittings from Italy, and aluminium window castings, air-conditioning units and elevators from the United States.

facts.fact: Built in a record 21 months, it became the largest hotel in Eastern Europe and the Middle East.
facts.quote: After completing the construction work in a record time of 21 months, the hotel became the largest in Eastern Europe and the Middle East.

facts.fact: KAPSARC is a research and advisory centre for energy economics, climate and sustainability in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.
facts.quote: The King Abdullah Petroleum Studies and Research Center (KAPSARC) is a research and advisory organization focusing on energy economics, climate and sustainability. It is located in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

facts.fact: The campus has a residential campus on the west and a research and office complex on the east.
facts.quote: The KAPSARC campus in Riyadh contains both a Residential Campus (called the REC, located on the west side) and a Research and Office Complex (called the ROC, on the east side).

facts.fact: The 70,000 square metre Research and Office Complex was designed by Zaha Hadid, who won the commission in a 2009 competition.
facts.quote: The 70,000 square meters Research and Office Complex was designed by Zaha Hadid, and supported by Event Communications. Hadid received the commission after a 2009 design competition.

facts.fact: It opened in October 2017 and received LEED Platinum certification.
facts.quote: It opened in October 2017 and received a LEED Platinum certification.

facts.fact: The complex is made of five interlocking buildings: a research centre, a computer centre, a conference centre, a library and a prayer hall (the Musalla).
facts.quote: The complex consists of five interlocking buildings, a research center, a computer center, a conference center, a library and the Musalla, a place for prayer.

facts.fact: The Education City Mosque is part of the Qatar Faculty of Islamic Studies, in the Minaretein building at Hamad Bin Khalifa University.
facts.quote: The mosque forms part of Qatar Faculty of Islamic Studies (QFIS), located in the Minaretein building, on the campus of the Hamad Bin Khalifa University.

facts.fact: The same building also holds teaching and faculty space and a research centre.
facts.quote: Also included in the building is teaching and faculty space and a research centre for the QFIS.

facts.fact: Designed by Mangera Yvars and completed in 2013, the building rests on five large columns standing for the five pillars of Islam, each bearing a verse of the Qur'an.
facts.quote: Designed by the architectural team of Mangera Yvars and completed in 2013, the QFIS Minaretein building rests on five large columns representing the five pillars of Islam, with each featuring a verse drawn from the Qur'an.

facts.fact: The design follows the Islamic idea of the kulliyya, with a spiral plan and paths linking the teaching spaces to the mosque; a four-storey ablution cascade under the mosque helps keep it cool.
facts.quote: The QFIS is based on the idea of the Islamic kulliyya, suggesting that all knowledge comes from faith, explored the infinite spiral form of the building plan and the pathways which link the teaching and learning spaces to the mosque, separated symbolically  by a four-storey ablution cascade under the mosque, that helps to keep the mosque cool.

facts.fact: It won Best Religious Building at the 2015 World Architecture Festival and was nominated for RIBA's first international prize.
facts.quote: The building won the 2015 Best Religious Building prize at the World Architecture Festival; and in the following year it was nominated by the Royal Institute of British Architects for its inaugural international prize.

facts.fact: It has also won several sustainability awards.
facts.quote: It has also won several sustainability awards.

facts.fact: The Nubian Museum in Aswan is an archaeological museum built after the UNESCO campaign to save the monuments of Nubia.
facts.quote: The Nubian Museum (officially the International Museum of Nubia) is an archaeological museum in Aswan, Upper Egypt. It was built in 23 November 1997 following the UNESCO International Campaign to Save the Monuments of Nubia.

facts.fact: It opened on 23 November 1997, won the Aga Khan Award for Architecture in 2001, and was designed by Egyptian architect Mahmoud El-Hakim.
facts.quote: Dedicated to Nubian culture, heritage, and civilization, it was inaugurated on November 23, 1997, and was awarded the Aga Khan Award for Architecture in 2001. The museum was designed by Egyptian architect Mahmoud El-Hakim.

facts.fact: The site covers 50,000 square metres, of which 7,000 are building and the rest gardens and public space.
facts.quote: The Nubian Museum covers an area of 50,000 square meters, 7,000 of which are devoted to the building, while the rest are devoted to gardens and other public spaces.

facts.fact: It is built of local stone on a rocky hill, and its plan and look draw on the region's ancient temples, fortresses and houses.
facts.quote: It is built of local stone on a rocky hill, and its plan and appearance draw on ancient temples, fortresses and the domestic architecture of the region.

facts.fact: The building has three floors for displays and storage, plus a library and information centre.
facts.quote: The building has three floors for displaying and housing, in addition to a library and information center.

facts.fact: Built on a steep cliff, the museum lays out a full-scale design of the Nile from its sources in Ethiopia and Sudan to Egypt.
facts.quote: The Museum is built on a steep cliff, which enables it to embody a full scale design for the Nile river from its origins in Ethiopia and Sudan to Egypt.

facts.fact: The building is surrounded by a botanical garden of Egyptian plants.
facts.quote: The edifice is surrounded by a Natural Botanical Garden, which contains a large variety of Egyptian flora.

facts.fact: The university, designed by Oscar Niemeyer, was founded in 1969.
facts.quote: Designed by Brazilian architect Oscar Niemeyer, the university was established in 1969.

facts.fact: It stands on the road from Mohamed Boudiaf Airport to the centre of Constantine.
facts.quote: The University is located in the city of Constantine, on the road connecting Mohamed Boudiaf Airport to the city center.

facts.fact: The 1969 decree made it independent of the University of Algiers, of which it had been a branch centre.
facts.quote: This is an important date for the university, as it gained its independence after having been a university center affiliated with the University of Algiers, whose mission was limited to teaching a limited number of disciplines such as literature and law.

facts.fact: The project was commissioned by President Houari Boumediene.
facts.quote: The project of the university was commissioned by President Houari Boumedienne, who remained in power from 1965 to 1978, and coordinated by the Minister of Higher Education and Scientific Research Seddik Benyahia (1971-1977).

facts.fact: It was built by the Ecotec company to Niemeyer's plans, with Niemeyer working with Ecotec's design office.
facts.quote: The university was designed according to the plans of Brazilian architect Oscar Niemeyer (who was in contact with the Ecotec design office headed by Mr. Mehnaoui Abdelhamid) and built by the Ecotec company.

facts.fact: The university is made up of more than six buildings.
facts.quote: The university consists of more than 6 buildings:

facts.fact: The concrete memorial to the Algerian War opened on 5 July 1982, the 20th anniversary of Algeria's independence.
facts.quote: The monument was opened on July 5, 1982, on the 20th anniversary of Algeria's independence.

facts.fact: It is shaped like three standing palm leaves that shelter an eternal flame.
facts.quote: It is fashioned in the shape of three standing palm leaves, which shelter the "Eternal Flame" under it.

facts.fact: A statue of a soldier at the foot of each leaf stands for a stage of the struggle for independence.
facts.quote: At the edge of each palm leaf is a statue of a soldier representing a stage of Algeria's struggle for independence.

facts.fact: The three fins join at mid-height and rise to 96 metres; it was built by the Canadian firm Lavalin from a model made at the Fine Art Institute of Algiers under Bashir Yellès.
facts.quote: Consisting of three stylized fins that join mid-height, the concrete monument built by the Canadian company Lavalin, based on a model produced in the Fine Art Institute of Algiers, under the leadership of Bashir Yelles, reaches a height of 96 metres (315 ft).

facts.fact: The esplanade holds the eternal flame, a crypt, an amphitheatre and an underground national museum.
facts.quote: It rests on an esplanade that burns an "eternal flame" and includes a crypt, an amphitheater and the National Museum of El Mujahid (underground).

facts.fact: Painter Bashir Yellès, calligrapher Abdelhamid Skander and Polish sculptor Marian Konieczny worked on it.
facts.quote: Several Algerian artists were involved, like the painter Bashir Yelles, the calligrapher Abdelhamid Skander and the Polish sculptor Marian Konieczny.

facts.fact: The curved fins, the clifftop site and the region's high seismic risk made it a technical challenge.
facts.quote: The completion of the work was a real technological challenge because of the constraints inherent to the geometry of the assembly, especially the curvature of the fins, the situation of the site at the edge of a steep cliff and high seismicity of the region.

facts.fact: It was built in under eight months, from 15 November 1981 to 5 July 1982.
facts.quote: Seven months (7 months and 20 days) (November 15, 1981 to July 5, 1982) were necessary to build this architectural work.

facts.fact: Kamalapur is the largest and busiest station in Bangladesh, the gateway to the capital.
facts.quote: It is the largest station and the busiest infrastructure for transportation in the country that acts as a gateway to the country's capital.

facts.fact: It opened in 1968.
facts.quote: It was opened on 1 May 1968.

facts.fact: Its architects were Americans Daniel Dunham and Bob Buie, who came to East Pakistan with the Louis Berger Group.
facts.quote: The architects of Kamalapur railway station were two Americans: Daniel Dunham and Bob Buie. Both came to East Pakistan as architects with the Louis Berger Group.

facts.fact: The design was begun under Dunham and continued by Robert Boughey.
facts.quote: The design process started under the direction of Dunham, followed by Robert Boughey.

facts.fact: They designed an unusual concrete parasol roof, a wide span suited to the climate.
facts.quote: For that, they designed a concrete structure for the station building roof that was unusual; the structure had a parasol roof.

facts.fact: Its rhythm of tapered, arched shells evokes an umbrella sheltering from monsoon rain.
facts.quote: The terminal's profile – a rhythmic arrangement of gently tapered and arched shells evokes the typical image of a tropical climate, with an umbrella providing protection from monsoon rains.

facts.fact: Ticket booths, offices and waiting areas all sit under one canopy roof.
facts.quote: The design of the station includes various functional spaces, including the station's ticket booth, administrative offices, passenger rest areas, and waiting areas under an integrated canopy roof.

facts.fact: The roof has 36 slender concrete domes, carried on columns 59 feet high that each branch into four arms.
facts.quote: Above it stands a roof with 36 slender concrete domes. Each column, 59 feet high, extends four branches upward and supports the roof.

facts.fact: The Gate of Europe is a pair of office towers near Plaza de Castilla in Madrid.
facts.quote: The Gate of Europe towers (Spanish: Puerta de Europa), also known as KIO Towers/"Door of Europa" (Torres KIO), are twin office buildings near the Plaza de Castilla in Madrid, Spain.

facts.fact: The towers have 26 floors and were built from 1989 to 1996.
facts.quote: The towers have a height of 114 m (374 ft) and have 26 floors. They were constructed from 1989 to 1996.

facts.fact: They were designed by Philip Johnson and John Burgee and commissioned by the Kuwait Investment Office, hence the name KIO Towers.
facts.quote: The Gate of Europe towers were designed by the American architects Philip Johnson and John Burgee, built by Fomento de Construcciones y Contratas and commissioned by the Kuwait Investment Office (hence their initial name "Torres KIO" or "KIO Towers").

facts.fact: Structural engineering was by Leslie E. Robertson Associates.
facts.quote: Leslie E. Robertson Associates, RLLP New York (LERA) provided structural engineering services.

facts.fact: Each tower leans at 15°, making them the first inclined skyscrapers in the world.
facts.quote: Each building is 115 m tall with an inclination of 15°, making them the first inclined skyscrapers in the world.

facts.fact: They stand on either side of the Plaza de Castilla bus station, near Chamartín station and the Cuatro Torres Business Area.
facts.quote: They are located near the Chamartín railway station, on the sides of the Plaza de Castilla bus station, north from the Paseo de la Castellana and near the Cuatro Torres Business Area (CTBA).

facts.fact: The towers are one of Philip Johnson's rare works in Europe, begun with John Burgee.
facts.quote: The Gate of Europe in Madrid (1989-1996) was originally a collaboration with Burgee and one of his rare works in Europe.

facts.fact: The SEC Armadillo, first called the Clyde Auditorium, is a concert and conference venue on the River Clyde in Glasgow.
facts.quote: The SEC Armadillo, originally known as the Clyde Auditorium, is a concert and conference venue located on the banks of the River Clyde in Glasgow, Scotland.

facts.fact: Designed by Foster + Partners, it opened in September 1997 as an expansion of the Scottish Exhibition and Conference Centre.
facts.quote: Designed by the architectural practice Foster + Partners, the building opened in September 1997 as an expansion of the Scottish Exhibition and Conference Centre (SECC).

facts.fact: Its overlapping curved shells gave it the popular nickname that became its name.
facts.quote: Its distinctive exterior, formed by a series of overlapping curved structures, led to its popular nickname, which subsequently became its recognised name.

facts.fact: It was part of the regeneration of Glasgow's former industrial waterfront.
facts.quote: The development of the SEC Armadillo formed part of the wider transformation of Glasgow's former industrial waterfront.

facts.fact: Construction began in September 1995, with structural engineering by Arup.
facts.quote: Construction began in September 1995, with the project forming part of the continuing expansion of the SECC complex. The structural engineering was undertaken by Arup, which provided engineering services for the building, including civil, structural, mechanical, electrical and geotechnical design.

facts.fact: The curved form and complex structure made it an engineering challenge; Arup's account describes a system of curved shells on supporting steelwork.
facts.quote: However, the engineering account published by Arup documents the structure's distinctive system of curved shells and supporting steelwork, demonstrating the technical complexity behind its appearance.

facts.fact: Its sculptural roofline has sometimes been compared with the Sydney Opera House.
facts.quote: The building has sometimes been compared visually with the Sydney Opera House because of its sculptural roofline.

facts.fact: The auditorium holds up to about 3,000 people, with seating that can be rearranged.
facts.quote: Its flexible seating arrangements allow it to be configured for events of different sizes, with a maximum capacity of approximately 3,000 people.

facts.fact: With the Prado and the Reina Sofía, the Thyssen-Bornemisza Museum forms Madrid's Golden Triangle of Art on the Paseo del Prado, a UNESCO World Heritage site since 2021.
facts.quote: The Prado and the nearby Thyssen-Bornemisza Museum and the Museo Reina Sofía form Madrid's Golden Triangle of Art along the Paseo del Prado, which was  added to the UNESCO World Heritage list in 2021.

facts.fact: The Nanjing International Youth Cultural Centre is a pair of skyscrapers in Nanjing designed by Zaha Hadid Architects.
facts.quote: Nanjing International Youth Cultural Center (Chinese: 南京国际青年文化中心) are two skyscrapers in Nanjing, Jiangsu, China designed by Zaha Hadid Architects.

facts.fact: Tower 1 is 314.5 m tall and Tower 2 is 255 m.
facts.quote: Tower 1 is 314.5 meters (1,032 ft) tall and Tower 2 is 255 meters (837 ft).

facts.fact: Construction ran from 2012 to 2015.
facts.quote: Construction began in 2012 and ended in 2015.

facts.fact: New Orleans is a 45-storey, 158.4 m residential tower in Rotterdam designed by Álvaro Siza.
facts.quote: New Orleans is a 45-storey, 158.4 m (520 ft) residential skyscraper in Rotterdam, Netherlands, designed by Álvaro Siza Vieira.

facts.fact: It was the tallest residential building in the Netherlands until De Zalmhaven was completed in 2022.
facts.quote: It was the tallest residential building (and second tallest building overall) in the Netherlands, until completion of the De Zalmhaven in 2022.

facts.fact: Besides flats with a pool, saunas and gym, it holds the LantarenVenster cinema.
facts.quote: Consist of residential area with swimming pool, saunas and gym for residents as well as commercial area with cinema LantarenVenster.

facts.fact: Generali Tower, nicknamed lo Storto ("the Twisted One"), is an office tower in Milan completed in 2017, 177.4 m tall with 44 floors.
facts.quote: Generali Tower, or Hadid Tower (lo Storto, "the Twisted One"), is an office skyscraper completed in 2017 in Milan, Italy that reaches a height of 177.4 m (582 ft) with 44 floors (+ 3 floors basement), and a total floor area of about 67,000 square metres (720,000 sq ft).

facts.fact: It was designed by Zaha Hadid.
facts.quote: Its designer is the Anglo-Iraqi architect Zaha Hadid, hence it is also called torre Hadid ("Hadid Tower").

facts.fact: The tower warps as it rises: both the size and the orientation of the floors change along its axis.
facts.quote: The geometry of the building is that of a warping shape, where both the dimensions of the floors and their orientation vary along the tower axis.

facts.fact: The structure is concrete and composite, with a central core as the main stiffening element.
facts.quote: The structure is concrete and composite. A central core acts as the main horizontal stiffening and resisting element.

facts.fact: It stands on a 2.5 m thick concrete raft resting on 64 piles.
facts.quote: The base raft is a 2.5-metre-thick (8.2 ft) concrete slab, resting on 64 piles arranged in clusters and points under the main load points.

facts.fact: A free-form steel podium for shops wraps the base.
facts.quote: A steel, free-form podium for commercial use surrounds the base of the building.

facts.fact: In 2019 the American Concrete Institute gave it first place for excellence in the high-rise category.
facts.quote: In October 2019, the tower was awarded first place for excellence in the high-rise category by the American Concrete Institute.

facts.fact: It houses offices of the insurer Assicurazioni Generali.
facts.quote: The building hosts offices of Assicurazioni Generali, the third largest insurance group in the world by revenue.

facts.fact: Our Lady of Meritxell is the patron saint of Andorra.
facts.quote: Our Lady of Meritxell is the patron saint of Andorra.

facts.fact: The old chapel that held the Romanesque statue burned down on 8 September 1972, and the new Meritxell Basilica, holding a replica, was designed in 1976 by Ricardo Bofill Taller de Arquitectura.
facts.quote: However, the chapel in which it was housed burned down on 8 September 1972, and the statue was destroyed. A replica can be found in the new Meritxell Basilica, designed in 1976 by Ricardo Bofill Taller de Arquitectura.

facts.fact: Herzog & de Meuron designed the tower for Hoffmann-La Roche; it is 178 m tall with 41 floors.
facts.quote: Designed by Herzog & de Meuron for the pharmaceutical company Hoffmann-La Roche, it stands 178 metres (584 ft) tall with 41 floors.

facts.fact: When it opened it was the tallest building in Switzerland.
facts.quote: At the time of its opening, it was the tallest building in Switzerland, surpassing the Prime Tower (126 meters) in Zürich by 52 metres.

facts.fact: It has 74,200 m² of floor space, cost CHF 550 million and holds about 2,000 staff.
facts.quote: The building has a total floor space of 74,200 m2 (799,000 sq ft) and cost CHF 550 million to construct. It houses around 2,000 employees.

facts.fact: Construction began in 2012 and it was inaugurated on 18 September 2015.
facts.quote: Construction of Building 1 began in 2012, and it was officially inaugurated on 18 September 2015.

facts.fact: It stands on 143 piles up to 24 m deep, under a foundation slab meant to add stability in earthquakes.
facts.quote: The structure stands on 143 piles driven up to 24 metres (79 ft) into the ground, topped by a foundation slab intended to enhance stability in earthquakes.

facts.fact: It was engineered for a magnitude 6.9 earthquake, above the legal requirement.
facts.quote: The tower was engineered to withstand a magnitude 6.9 earthquake on the Richter scale, a standard higher than legally required, corresponding to an event statistically expected once every 1,500 years.

facts.fact: A closed-cavity facade gives solar shading and outward views and needs less cleaning.
facts.quote: The building features a closed-cavity facade that reduces cleaning requirements, provides solar shading, and maintains outward visibility.

facts.fact: Heating, cooling and ventilation use groundwater cooling and waste-heat recovery.
facts.quote: The heating, cooling, and ventilation systems use groundwater cooling along with waste-heat recovery.

facts.fact: Place Ville Marie is an office and shopping complex in downtown Montreal: four office buildings and an underground shopping plaza.
facts.quote: Place Ville Marie (French pronunciation: [plas vil maʁi], abbr. PVM) is a large office and shopping complex skyscraper in Downtown Montreal, Quebec, Canada, comprising four office buildings and an underground shopping plaza.

facts.fact: The main tower was built in the International Style in 1962 as the Royal Bank of Canada's headquarters.
facts.quote: The main building, 1 Place Ville Marie (formerly Royal Bank Tower from its anchor tenant), was built in the International style in 1962 as the headquarters for the Royal Bank of Canada.

facts.fact: It is a 188 m, 47-storey cruciform office tower.
facts.quote: It is a 188 m (617 ft), 47-storey, cruciform office tower.

facts.fact: The complex is a hub of Montreal's Underground City.
facts.quote: The complex is a nexus for Montreal's Underground City (RÉSO), the world's busiest, with indoor access to over 1,600 businesses, numerous subway stations, a suburban transportation terminal, and tunnels extending throughout downtown.

facts.fact: It was built over a railway trench, so the structure had to resist vibration, making it Montreal's most earthquake-resistant office tower.
facts.quote: Most of the building was thus built over the tracks, requiring the structure to be more resistant to vibrations than normally required. As a result, it is the most earthquake-resistant office tower in Montreal.

facts.fact: It was one of the first built projects of Henry N. Cobb, and the design was controversial from the start.
facts.quote: Place Ville Marie was one of the first built projects of Henry N. Cobb, a founding partner of Pei Cobb Freed & Partners. His design was controversial from the start, given its proximity to many Montreal landmarks and the vast changes it would bring to the downtown core.

facts.fact: Nearly half of its area was below street level, sheltered from Montreal's harsh winters and summers.
facts.quote: According to design historian Mark Pimlott, "The most radical aspect of the Place Ville Marie project was that nearly one-half of its 280,000-square-metre area was beneath street level [...] deriving the obvious benefit of being protected from Montréal’s extreme winter and summer climate."

facts.fact: When built, the main tower was the tallest skyscraper in the Commonwealth.
facts.quote: At the time of construction, the main tower was known as the tallest skyscraper in the Commonwealth, and was the third tallest skyscraper on Earth outside the United States.

facts.fact: Tour de la Bourse is a 48-storey skyscraper on Victoria Square in Montreal.
facts.quote: The Tour de la Bourse (lit. 'Stock Exchange Tower') is a 48-storey skyscraper in Montreal, Quebec, Canada. It is located at the intersection of Victoria Square and Saint Jacques Street in the International Quarter.

facts.fact: When completed in 1964 it was the tallest building in Canada, until 1967.
facts.quote: When completed in 1964, the tower was the tallest building in Canada, a title it held until surpassed by the Toronto-Dominion Centre in 1967.

facts.fact: It was designed by Luigi Moretti and Pier Luigi Nervi in the International Style.
facts.quote: The Tour de la Bourse was designed by Luigi Moretti and Pier Luigi Nervi and is considered to be of the International Style.

facts.fact: The first plan, from the Expo 67 boom years, called for three identical towers arranged in a triangle.
facts.quote: The original project, conceived during the Expo 67-era economic boom, called for three identical towers arrayed in a triangle.

facts.fact: Its bronze-tinted aluminium curtain wall contrasts with slightly slanted pre-cast concrete columns at the four corners, giving a subtly convex look.
facts.quote: Its façade, fully renovated in 1995, features a bronze-tinted anodized aluminium curtain wall, forming a strong contrast with the slightly slanted pre-cast concrete columns at the four corners, giving the whole a subtly convex aspect.

facts.fact: Mechanical floors with recessed octagonal corners divide it into three blocks, leaving open-air gaps behind the columns.
facts.quote: It is divided into three roughly equal blocks by mechanical floors whose corners are recessed in an octagonal shape, creating small open-air interstices behind the columns at these levels.

facts.fact: At 190 m it was the world's tallest reinforced concrete tower until 1968.
facts.quote: This 190 m (620 ft), 48-story building was the world's tallest reinforced concrete tower until the completion of Lake Point Tower in Chicago in 1968, and the tallest building in Canada until the completion of Toronto-Dominion Centre in 1967.

facts.fact: Its anchor tenant is still the Montreal Exchange.
facts.quote: The building's anchor tenant is still the Montreal Exchange on floors 3 and 4.

facts.fact: The Kyushu National Museum opened on 16 October 2005 in Dazaifu, near Fukuoka: Japan's first new national museum in over 100 years, and the first to put history before art.
facts.quote: The Kyushu National Museum (九州国立博物館, Kyūshū Kokuritsu Hakubutsukan) opened on October 16, 2005, in Dazaifu near Fukuoka—the first new national museum in Japan in over 100 years, and the first to elevate the focus on history over art.

facts.fact: The museum was designed by Kiyonori Kikutake.
facts.quote: The museum was designed by Kiyonori Kikutake.

facts.fact: The site is next to the Dazaifu Tenman-gū shrine.
facts.quote: The site is next to the Dazaifu Tenman-gū.

facts.fact: The wood and glass building in the hills holds Japanese artefacts, especially ceramics, on the history of Kyushu.
facts.quote: The striking wood and glass building in the hills, it hosts important collections of Japanese artifacts, particularly ceramics, related to the history of Kyūshū.

facts.fact: Temporary exhibitions are on the third floor and the permanent collection on the fourth.
facts.quote: It hosts temporary exhibitions on the third floor, while the permanent collections are on the fourth floor.

facts.fact: The collections trace Kyushu from prehistory to the Meiji era, stressing its exchange with China and Korea.
facts.quote: The collections cover the history of Kyūshū from prehistory to the Meiji era with particular emphasis on the rich history of cultural exchange between Kyūshū and neighboring China and Korea.

facts.fact: It has its own conservation labs and serves as the main conservation centre for western Japan.
facts.quote: Unlike most museums in Japan, which contract out conservation work, the Kyushu National Museum has an extensive on-site suite of conservation labs and associated staff, serving as the major conservation center for all of western Japan.

facts.fact: Work on the building was finished in 2004.
facts.quote: 2004—Work on the building is completed.

facts.fact: The Muziekgebouw aan 't IJ is Amsterdam's main concert hall for contemporary classical music, on the IJ waterfront.
facts.quote: Muziekgebouw aan 't IJ (English: "Music Building on the IJ") is the main concert hall for contemporary classical music on the IJ in Amsterdam, Netherlands.

facts.fact: It opened in 2005, sits above the IJtunnel and is a ten-minute walk from Amsterdam Centraal.
facts.quote: The building opened in 2005 and is located above the IJtunnel, a ten-minute walk from Amsterdam Centraal station.

facts.fact: It was designed by the Danish architects 3XN.
facts.quote: The building was designed by Danish architects 3XN.

facts.fact: The Bimhuis is part of the building and partly built into it.
facts.quote: The Bimhuis is part of and partly integrated in the Muziekgebouw aan 't IJ.

facts.fact: There is one large concert hall and a smaller one, and concerts also take place in the atrium and on three large balconies above the restaurant.
