facts.quote: Muziekgebouw aan 't IJ has one big concert space, but also a smaller one that is also used for conferences, talk, exhibitions. Also concerts take place at various other locations in the building such as the atrium and on the three large balconies above the restaurant.

facts.fact: The small hall houses a 31-tone Fokker organ.
facts.quote: Inside the Kleine Zaal (previously known as Bamzaal) there is also the microtonal 31-TET Fokker organ, designed by Adriaan Fokker.

facts.fact: It won an Urban Land Institute Award for Excellence (Europe) in 2006.
facts.quote: Urban Land Institute Award for Excellence, category Europe (2006)

facts.fact: Tokyo Sea Life Park is a public aquarium in Kasai Rinkai Park, Edogawa, Tokyo, successor to the Ueno Aquarium.
facts.quote: Tokyo Sea Life Park (葛西臨海水族園, kasai-rinkai-suizoku-en) is a public aquarium located in Kasai Rinkai Park, Edogawa Ward, Tokyo. Its predecessor was the Ueno Aquarium in the Ueno Zoo.

facts.fact: The building was designed by Yoshio Taniguchi.
facts.quote: The building was designed by Yoshio Taniguchi.

facts.fact: Planned for the centenary of Ueno Zoo as Japan's largest aquarium, it opened in 1989.
facts.quote: In commemoration of the centenary of Ueno Zoo, a plan was unveiled to build the largest aquarium in Japan. The new aquarium officially opened in 1989 as Tokyo Sea Life Park.

facts.fact: About 650 species live in 47 tanks, including tuna in a large round tank viewed from its centre.
facts.quote: Approximately 650 species are kept in 47 tanks, including tuna that inhabit a large, round tank with a viewing area in its center.

facts.fact: It drew 3.55 million visitors in its first year, a Japanese record at the time.
facts.quote: The annual number of visitors in the first year of the park reached 3.55 million, far exceeding the Japanese record at that time (2.4 million at Suma Aqualife Park in 1987).

facts.fact: Its ring-shaped 2,200 m³ tank was the largest indoor tank in Japan when built in 1989.
facts.quote: Voyagers of the Sea – A ring-shaped 2,200 m3 (580,000 US gal) tank. It was the largest indoor tank in Japan when it was built in 1989.

facts.fact: In January 2019 the park drew up a basic plan for a new facility on the site.
facts.quote: In January 2019, the park formulated a basic plan for a new facility on the premises.

facts.fact: Tour Perret is a 29-storey, 110 m residential tower in Amiens, described as France's first skyscraper and listed as a historic monument in 1975.
facts.quote: Tour Perret ('Perret Tower') is a 29-storey, 110 m (360 ft) residential skyscraper in Amiens, France. It has been described as France's first skyscraper, and was registered as a historic monument in 1975.

facts.fact: It was part of Auguste Perret's large reconstruction project around Place Alphonse-Fiquet, which also rebuilt the nearby railway station.
facts.quote: Its building was part of a large scale reconstruction project helmed by architect Auguste Perret in the Place Alphone-Fiquet neighborhood, which also involved a rebuild of the nearby railway station.

facts.fact: Design began in 1942, after heavy wartime damage to central Amiens; Perret wanted an office building but was overruled.
facts.quote: The design phase started as early as 1942, following extensive damages suffered by downtown Amiens during World War II. Perret intended it as an office building before authorities overruled him.

facts.fact: At 104 m it was the first skyscraper over 100 m built in France.
facts.quote: Originally measuring 104 metres, Tour Perret was the highest, and the first 100-plus metre skyscraper built in France, although it was not the highest in Western Europe, as it has sometimes been written.

facts.fact: Its planned top, a belfry with a large clock, was never built because of delays and cost overruns.
facts.quote: The building actually fell slightly short of its intended height as its topmost part, a belfry adorned with a monumental clock, was never built due to delays and cost overruns.

facts.fact: In 2005 it was topped with the Hourglass of Light by Thierry Van de Wyngaert, a cube of 192 glass panels whose transparency can be adjusted.
facts.quote: In 2005, the tower was finally completed with a so-called Sablier de lumière (English: Hourglass of Light) designed by architect Thierry Van de Wyngaert. It is a cube made of 192 active glass panels whose transparency can be electrically adjusted, illuminated by twelve circular neon lamps which project different colors depending on the time of day.

facts.fact: Rohm Theatre Kyoto, officially Kyoto Kaikan, is a concert hall and performance venue in Kyoto.
facts.quote: Rohm Theatre Kyoto, officially known as Kyoto Kaikan, is a concert hall and performance venue located in Kyoto, Japan.

facts.fact: The main hall first opened in 1960 with 2,005 seats.
facts.quote: The main hall was first opened in 1960 and seated 2,005 patrons.

facts.fact: It closed in 2012 and was redeveloped over four years, reopening in January 2016.
facts.quote: The facility closed in 2012 and was redeveloped over a four-year period, reopening in January 2016.

facts.fact: Besides the main hall it has two smaller spaces for 700 and 200.
facts.quote: As well as the main concert hall, the facility also has two additional performance spaces seating 700 and 200 guests.

facts.fact: The Kyoto company Rohm gave ¥5.25 billion to the refurbishment, saving the landmark building from possible demolition, and received the naming rights.
facts.quote: Kyoto-based Rohm semiconductor saved the landmark post-modernist building from possible demolition by granting ¥5.25 billion towards the cost of refurbishment. In recognition of this contribution, Rohm received naming rights to the building.

facts.fact: Raffles City Chongqing is eight skyscrapers on a 9.2-hectare site in Yuzhong District, at the tip of the peninsula where the Yangtze and Jialing rivers meet.
facts.quote: Raffles City Chongqing consists of eight skyscrapers situated on a site covering 9.2 hectares, in Yuzhong District, at the tip of the peninsula where the Yangtze and Jialing Rivers meet.

facts.fact: It was designed by architect Moshe Safdie, who also designed the similar-looking Marina Bay Sands in Singapore.
facts.quote: The project was designed by architect Moshe Safdie, who also designed Singapore's similar-looking Marina Bay Sands.

facts.fact: The design was inspired by Chinese sailing vessels, as a tribute to Chongqing's past as a trading centre.
facts.quote: It was inspired by Chinese sailing vessels and is a tribute to Chongqing's historical past as a trading centre.

facts.fact: The Crystal is an enclosed horizontal skyway, 300 metres long, sitting on top of four of the towers.
facts.quote: The Crystal is an enclosed 300-metre-long horizontal skyway that sits atop four of the buildings.

facts.fact: The Crystal's exterior is made of about 3,000 glass panels and nearly 5,000 aluminium panels.
facts.quote: The exterior consists of approximately 3,000 glass panels and nearly 5,000 aluminum panels.

facts.fact: The buildings are reinforced concrete, with concrete-encased steel columns and steel floor spans.
facts.quote: The buildings are reinforced concrete with concrete-encased steel columns and steel floor spanning.

facts.fact: The complex mixes offices, 1,400 homes, a hotel, a shopping mall and landscaped grounds.
facts.quote: The project contains 1.12 million square metres of space, 817,000 square metres of which is floor space and includes 150,000m2 of office space and 1,400 residences, a hotel, a 235,000m2 shopping mall, and landscaped grounds.

facts.fact: Raffles City Chongqing won the China Tall Building Innovation Award.
facts.quote: Raffles City Chongqing won the China Tall Building Innovation Award.

facts.fact: Zorlu Center is a mixed-use complex of high-rise buildings in Istanbul's Beşiktaş district, with a shopping mall, a hotel, a cinema, homes and offices.
facts.quote: Zorlu Center is a mixed-use high-rise building complex in the Beşiktaş district of Istanbul, Turkey containing an upscale shopping mall, a five-star Raffles hotel and a Cinemaximum megaplex, as well as residences and offices.

facts.fact: It was built in 2013 to a design by Emre Arolat Architects and Tabanlıoğlu Architects, at the junction of the Bosphorus Bridge's European approach and Barbaros Boulevard.
facts.quote: Built in 2013 to a design by Emre Arolat Architects and Tabanlıoğlu Architects, the center is situated at the junction of the European connection of the Bosphorus Bridge with Barbaros Boulevard, which proceeds to the north as Büyükdere Avenue in Levent and Maslak.

facts.fact: Over 100 firms applied to the design competition; 13 were chosen to take part, and Tabanlıoğlu Architects and Emre Arolat Architects won.
facts.quote: Over 100 firms applied and 13 were selected to take part in the competition with Tabanlıoğlu Architects and Emre Arolat Architects submitting the winning proposal.

facts.fact: The centre is a group of four towers serving five functions, including a public square, homes, a hotel and offices.
facts.quote: The center is a four-tower, five-function structure group, including a public square, residential development, hotel, and office space.

facts.fact: The design is based on the idea of a historic town square, with bold geometric lines framing the sky and large areas of greenery.
facts.quote: The design is stated to be "shaped by a modern understanding of architecture", based on the concept of a historical town square, incorporating "bold geometric lines that frame the sky, as well as large expanses of greenery".

facts.fact: It holds Zorlu PSM, the largest performing arts centre in Turkey.
facts.quote: It is home to Zorlu PSM, the largest performing arts center in the country, as well as the country's first Apple Store.

facts.fact: Zorlu PSM has a 770-seat theatre and a 2,300-seat concert hall.
facts.quote: It features a 770-seat theater as well as a 2,300-seat concert hall.

facts.fact: Torre BBVA México is an office skyscraper on Paseo de la Reforma in Colonia Juárez, Mexico City.
facts.quote: The Torre BBVA México ("BBVA México Tower", formerly Torre BBVA Bancomer) is an office skyscraper on Paseo de la Reforma in Colonia Juárez, Mexico City.

facts.fact: It is the headquarters of BBVA México, the country's largest bank.
facts.quote: It is the headquarters of BBVA México, Mexico's largest bank and a subsidiary of Spanish financial company Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria (BBVA).

facts.fact: When completed in 2015 it was the second-tallest building in Mexico City, 235 metres high with 50 storeys.
facts.quote: Upon its completion in 2015 it became the second tallest building in Mexico City at 235 metres (771 ft) and 50 stories high.

facts.fact: It was designed by LegoRogers, a collaboration between Legorreta + Legorreta and Rogers Stirk Harbour + Partners.
facts.quote: The building was designed by LegoRogers, which is a collaboration between the architectural practices of Legorreta + Legorreta and Rogers Stirk Harbour + Partners.

facts.fact: The Lighthouse is the renamed, A-listed conversion of the former offices of the Glasgow Herald newspaper.
facts.quote: The Lighthouse is the renamed, A-listed conversion of the former offices of the Glasgow Herald newspaper.

facts.fact: The building was officially designed by Honeyman and Keppie, with Charles Rennie Mackintosh contributing; it was his first building for the firm.
facts.quote: It was officially designed by architecture firm Honeyman and Keppie; one of the contributing artists was Charles Rennie Mackintosh. It was his first building for the firm.

facts.fact: The design draws on Scottish baronial and Queen Anne styles, and its proportions and windows are seen as typical of Mackintosh.
facts.quote: The design includes features from the Scottish baronial and Queen Anne styles, and the building's proportions and window arrangements are considered to be characteristic of Mackintosh's architectural work.

facts.fact: Construction began in February 1894 and was finished by summer 1895.
facts.quote: Construction began in February 1894 and was completed by summer 1895.

facts.fact: Mackintosh also worked on the interiors; the editor's room shows his influence most strongly.
facts.quote: Mackintosh also contributed to the building's interior design: the editor's room has been identified as a space that showed his influence particularly strongly.

facts.fact: The Glasgow Herald occupied the building until 1980, when it moved to Albion Street.
facts.quote: The Glasgow Herald occupied the building until 1980, when it moved location to Albion Street.

facts.fact: After a £13 million renovation and extension by Page and Park Architects, it reopened in July 1999 as The Lighthouse, Scotland's Centre for Architecture and Design.
facts.quote: It underwent renovations and extensions by Page and Park Architects costing £13 million, and was reopened in July 1999 by Queen Elizabeth II. It was renamed The Lighthouse, Scotland's Centre for Architecture and Design.

facts.fact: A spiral staircase leads to an outdoor platform with views of the city centre.
facts.quote: Furthermore, a spiral staircase lead to an outdoor platform that boasted views of the city centre and a rooftop café-bar.

facts.fact: Tokyo Skytree is a broadcasting and observation tower in Sumida, Tokyo.
facts.quote: Tokyo Skytree (東京スカイツリー, Tōkyō Sukaitsurī; [tò̞ó̞.kʲjó̞ó̞ (|) sɯ̥̈.kä́í.t͡sɯ̈́.ɾʲíì, tó̞ó̞.-] ), a.k.a Tokyo Sky Tree, is a broadcasting and observation tower, located in Sumida, Tokyo, Japan.

facts.fact: Nikken Sekkei was the main architectural firm for the Tokyo Skytree.
facts.quote: Osaka Library, 1904 Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation Osaka Head Office, 1930 Tokyo Tower, 1958 San'ai Dream Center, Tokyo, 1963 Shinjuku NS Building, Tokyo, 1982 Tokyo Dome, 1988 Trade Tower, Seoul, South Korea, 1988 Cairo Opera House, 1988 Pacifico Yokohama, 1991 Islamic development Bank Headquarters, Jeddah, 1993 Dubai Chamber of Commerce building, 1995 Queen's Square Yokohama, 1997 Saitama Super Arena, 2000 Bank of China Tower, 2000 Kyoto State Guest House, 2005 Tokyo Midtown, 2007 Hoki Museum, 2010 The Ritz-Carlton Kyoto, 2013 Guangzhou Library, 2013 Ruentex Nangang Station Complex, 2014 YKK 80 Building, 2015 Tokyo Plaza Ginza, 2016 Ariake Gymnastics Centre, 2019 One Za'abeel, 2024 H&S Residence, 2025 Trump International Hotel and Tower, 2031 Among other notable projects, Nikken Sekkei was the primary architectural firm for the Tokyo Skytree, currently (2019) the tallest self-supporting broadcasting tower in the world, and second tallest man made structure of any kind.

facts.fact: It was completed on 29 February 2012 and opened to the public on 22 May 2012.
facts.quote: Skytree was completed on Leap Day, 29 February 2012, with the tower opening to the public on 22 May 2012.

facts.fact: The design, published in 2006, aimed to fuse neofuturistic design with traditional Japanese beauty; the base is tripod-like and above about 350 m the structure becomes cylindrical.
facts.quote: The tower's design was published on 24 November 2006, based on the following three concepts: Fusion of neofuturistic design and the traditional beauty of Japan Catalyst for revitalization of the city Contribution to disaster prevention – "Safety and Security" The base of the tower has a structure similar to a tripod; from a height of about 350 m (1,150 ft) and above, the tower's structure is cylindrical to offer panoramic views of the river and the city.

facts.fact: For earthquake safety it has a central shaft of reinforced concrete.
facts.quote: The tower has seismic proofing, including a central shaft made of reinforced concrete.

facts.fact: Between 125 m and 375 m the central pillar is joined to the tower frame by oil dampers that act as cushions in an earthquake.
facts.quote: From there until 375 m (1,230 ft), the pillar is attached to the tower frame with oil dampers, which act as cushions during an earthquake.

facts.fact: The steel lattice is painted "Skytree White", a colour based on the traditional bluish-white Japanese colour aijiro.
facts.quote: The exterior lattice is painted a color officially called "Skytree White". This is an original color based on a bluish-white traditional Japanese color called aijiro (藍白).

facts.fact: Its height of 634 m was chosen because the digits 6-3-4 can be read as "Musashi", an old name for the region.
facts.quote: The height of 634 m (2,080 ft) was selected to be easily remembered based on numeric substitution. The figures 6 (mu), 3 (sa), 4 (shi) stand for "Musashi", an old name for the region where the Tokyo Skytree stands.

facts.fact: The Yokosuka Museum of Art opened in 2007 in Kannonzaki Park, Yokosuka, Kanagawa Prefecture.
facts.quote: Yokosuka Museum of Art (横須賀美術館, Yokosuka bijutsukan) opened in Kannonzaki Park (観音崎公園), Yokosuka, Kanagawa Prefecture, Japan, in 2007.

facts.fact: Its architect is Riken Yamamoto.
facts.quote: Architect: Riken Yamamoto.

facts.fact: Its collection of some 5,000 pieces includes works by Fujishima Takeji and Nakamura Tsune.
facts.quote: The collection, numbering some 5,000 pieces, includes works by Fujishima Takeji and Nakamura Tsune.

facts.fact: Riken Yamamoto received the Japan Institute of Architects Award (2010) and the Building Contractors Society Prize (2008) for the Yokosuka Museum of Art.
facts.quote: Under the many awards Riken Yamamoto has won, the most recent achieved by him are: The Japan Institute of Architects Award for the Yokosuka Museum of Art (2010) Building Contractors Society Prize for the Namics Techno Core (2010), Building Contractors Society Prize for the Yokosuka Museum of Art (2008) or the 25th Fukushima Architecture Culture Award, highest award for the Fukushima ecoms Pavilion, SUS Fukushima Factory (2007).

facts.fact: The Svaneke water tower, on the Danish island of Bornholm, was designed by Jørn Utzon and completed in 1952.
facts.quote: The Svaneke water tower, in the small town of Svaneke on the Danish island of Bornholm, was designed by award-winning architect Jørn Utzon and completed in 1952.

facts.fact: It was the first successful project of the architect who later designed the Sydney Opera House.
facts.quote: It was the first successful project of the architect who would later design the Sydney Opera House.

facts.fact: Utzon first sketched his idea on a paper serviette.
facts.quote: Utzon immediately sketched out his innovative idea on a paper serviette.

facts.fact: Its unusual shape was inspired by old sea marks used to help ships navigate.
facts.quote: The surprisingly shaped water tower was inspired by the old sea marks used for assisting the navigation of ships at sea.

facts.fact: The pyramid-shaped water tank sits on three slender reinforced-concrete legs that meet at the top, with concrete steps winding up in the middle.
facts.quote: The pyramidal water tank is supported by three slender ferro-concrete legs which meet at the top of the tower. The centrally placed steps, also made of concrete, wind up elegantly from the ground.

facts.fact: The tower was taken out of service in 1988 and has been a listed building since 1990.
facts.quote: The water tower was taken out of service in 1988 when alterations to the water supply system were introduced. Since 1990, it has been a listed building.

facts.fact: It was the first of five works by Utzon that can be called concrete architecture.

facts.fact: The Estadio Universitario is a baseball stadium next to the Olympic Stadium on the university campus, home to two teams.
