facts.fact: It rises 100 metres from the bottom of the canyon and is joined to the other side by a 50-metre-tall bridge.
facts.quote: It rises 100 m (330 ft) high from the bottom of the canyon and is connected to the opposite side of the canyon by a 50 m (160 ft) tall bridge.

facts.fact: It is a popular pilgrimage site for people from Colombia and neighbouring Ecuador, because of a Marian apparition said to have happened in the 18th century.
facts.quote: It is a popular pilgrimage site for Christians from both Colombia and neighboring Ecuador, due to a Marian apparition that is purported to have taken place in the 18th century.

facts.fact: The first shrine here, from the mid-18th century, was made of straw and wood, and was replaced by a 7-metre brick chapel in 1795/96.
facts.quote: The first shrine was built here in the middle of 18th century from straw and wood. It was replaced with a 7 meter long brick chapel in 1795/96.

facts.fact: Istanbul Modern is a contemporary art museum inside the Galataport complex in Istanbul's Beyoğlu district.
facts.quote: Istanbul Museum of Modern Art, colloquially referred to as Istanbul Modern (Turkish: İstanbul Modern Sanat Müzesi), is a contemporary art gallery located inside the Galataport complex in the Beyoğlu district of Istanbul, Turkey.

facts.fact: It first opened in December 2004 as Turkey's first museum of modern and contemporary art.
facts.quote: Inaugurated on December 11, 2004, Istanbul Modern was Turkey's first modern and contemporary art gallery and focuses on Turkish as well as international artists.

facts.fact: On 4 May 2023 it reopened in a new building near its original site in Karaköy, designed by Pritzker Prize winner Renzo Piano.
facts.quote: On 4 May 2023, the museum reopened in a new, state-of-the-art building close to its original location in Karaköy designed by the world-renowned, Pritzker Prize-winning architect Renzo Piano.

facts.fact: Piano imagined the building as a "flying vessel right on the water"; it has five storeys and 10,500 square metres of space.
facts.quote: Piano envisioned the structure as a "flying vessel right on the water."The five-story, 10,500 m2 (113,000 sq ft) building offers various exhibition halls as well as educational workshops, a cinema, a library, a design shop, event spaces, and a café and restaurant.

facts.fact: The ground floor is highly transparent, linking the museum to the Galataport promenade and Tophane Square.
facts.quote: Piano's design features a highly transparent ground floor that fosters a direct connection with the surrounding urban environment, including the renewed GalataPort promenade and Tophane Square.

facts.fact: The facade is made of 300 grey concave and convex aluminium modules, which Piano likened to "a fish leaping out of the water", catching light reflected from the Bosphorus.
facts.quote: The facade of Istanbul Modern, composed of 300 gray, concave, and convex aluminum modules that Piano likened to "a fish leaping out of the water", serves as a dynamic element interacting with changing light and reflections from the Bosphorus.

facts.fact: A central staircase is the main circulation spine through the museum's levels.
facts.quote: A staircase situated at the center serves as the main circulation spine, organizing movement across the museum's three levels.

facts.fact: A rooftop terrace looks over the historic peninsula and Galata Tower, with a 5 cm deep reflecting pool that mirrors the sky.
facts.quote: The rooftop terrace situated at the second floor offers panoramic views of Istanbul's historic peninsula and the Galata Tower. The terrace includes a 5 centimeter deep "Reflection Pool," which creates a visual extension of the Bosphorus by mirroring the sky and the surrounding cityscape.

facts.fact: The Florya Atatürk Marine Mansion is a historic presidential residence standing offshore in the Sea of Marmara, in Istanbul's Florya neighbourhood.
facts.quote: Florya Atatürk Marine Mansion (Turkish: Florya Atatürk Deniz Köşkü) is a historic presidential residence located offshore in the Sea of Marmara in the Florya neighborhood of the Bakırköy district in Istanbul, Turkey.

facts.fact: It was built in 1935 by the municipality of Istanbul for Atatürk's recreation.
facts.quote: It was built in 1935 by the municipality of Istanbul for Mustafa Kemal Atatürk's recreational use.

facts.fact: It was designed in the Bauhaus style by architect Seyfi Arkan and completed on 14 August 1935.
facts.quote: Designed in the Bauhaus style by architect Seyfi Arkan, who was given the commission in 1935 by the municipality of Istanbul, the mansion was completed on August 14 the same year, and was gifted to Atatürk.

facts.fact: It stands on steel piles driven into the seabed and is reached from the beach, about 70 metres away, by a wooden pier.
facts.quote: The building is constructed on steel piles driven into the seabed and is connected to the sandy beach about 70 m (230 ft) away with a wooden pier.

facts.fact: The L-shaped, single-storey house has a reception hall, a reading room, bedrooms and a bathroom.
facts.quote: The L-shaped, one-floor mansion consists of a reception hall, a reading room, bedrooms and bathroom.

facts.fact: It is considered an example of Turkish Early Republican architecture.
facts.quote: The mansion is considered an example of "Turkish Early Republican architecture".

facts.fact: Atatürk used it in the last three years of his life as a summer office and for recreation.
facts.quote: He used the mansion for the last three years of his life as a summer office as well as for recreation.

facts.fact: It was renovated and opened to the public as a museum in 1993.
facts.quote: It was then renovated and opened in 1993 to the public as a museum.

facts.fact: The Palace of Serbia is a government building in New Belgrade that houses several ministries and hosts state visits.
facts.quote: The Palace of Serbia (Serbian: Палата Србије, romanized: Palata Srbije) is a government building currently housing several government ministries and site for state visits of foreign head of states to Serbia.

facts.fact: The winning competition design, by a Zagreb team led by Vladimir Potočnjak, set the building's H-shaped exterior.
facts.quote: The accepted project from the group of architects from Zagreb included the exterior 'H' shape designed by lead architect Vladimir Potočnjak and his team: Anton Urlih, Zlatko Nojman and Dragica Perak.

facts.fact: Mihailo Janković took over the project, designed the interior and oversaw construction from 1955 until completion in 1959.
facts.quote: The project was taken over by Mihailo Janković who designed the interior of the structure and oversaw its construction when the construction works resumed works in 1955 until completion in 1959.

facts.fact: The original plans followed Socialist Realism, but after the 1948 Tito–Stalin split Janković's new design was modernist instead.
facts.quote: The original plans were designed according to the Socialist realism aesthetics, as Yugoslavia at that time was an ally of the Soviet Union. However, after the Tito–Stalin split in 1948, many things in the state changed, so the new project by Janković was Modernistic instead.

facts.fact: Its H-shaped plan covers about 65,000 square metres, making it the largest building by area in Serbia.
facts.quote: Its H-shaped base covers an area of approximately 65,000 m2 (700,000 sq ft) thus making Palace of Serbia the largest building by area in the country.

facts.fact: It has a reinforced concrete frame filled with brick, and its facade is clad in white Brač marble.
facts.quote: The building was constructed according to the system of the reinforced concrete skeleton structure, filled with bricks. The façade of the building is covered with the white Brač marble, whereas the openings were made of white metal.

facts.fact: A lower Central Annex under a glass dome holds the Main Salon, with room for 2,000 guests.
facts.quote: In front of the medium wing there is a Central Annex, lower area covered with the glass dome where the Main Salon is located, covering 8,000 m2 (86,000 sq ft) with capacity of 2,000 invitees.

facts.fact: Its interior, also designed by Janković, makes it a pioneering example of "total design" in Yugoslav architecture.
facts.quote: The representative exterior matches the luxuriously designed interior, also realized according to the architect Mihailo Janković's design, which places this building among the pioneer examples of the „total design“ in domestic architecture.

facts.fact: The Museum of the Future is a seven-floor building in Dubai's Financial District, devoted to the future of science, technology and innovation.
facts.quote: Museum of the Future (Arabic: متحف المستقبل) is a building located in the Financial District of Dubai, UAE. The museum, with 7 floors, is dedicated to exploring the future of science, technology, and innovation.

facts.fact: It is housed in a torus-shaped building whose windows form an Arabic poem about the future by Dubai's ruler.
facts.quote: It is housed in a torus-shaped building with windows in the form of a poem in Arabic about the future, written by Dubai ruler Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum.

facts.fact: It opened on 22 February 2022.
facts.quote: The Government of the United Arab Emirates opened the museum on 22 February 2022.

facts.fact: Killa Design won the design competition for the museum in 2015.
facts.quote: In 2015, Killa Design won the design competition for the Museum of the Future.

facts.fact: Said to be one of the world's most complex structures, it was designed by Shaun Killa Design and engineered by Buro Happold.
facts.quote: Claimed to be one of the world's most complex structures, the Museum of the Future was designed by UAE architectural firm Shaun Killa Design and engineered by Buro Happold.

facts.fact: The torus-shaped shell is made of 1,024 fire-retardant composite panels clad in stainless steel, each with a unique 3D shape to form the Arabic script.
facts.quote: The torus-shaped shell sits on top of the building and comprises 1,024 fire-retardant composite panels clad in stainless steel, and each of which has a unique 3D shape to create the Arabic script.

facts.fact: The designers developed new parametric and BIM tools, including a growth algorithm used to generate the internal steel structure.
facts.quote: Killa Design and Buro Happold developed new parametric design and building information modelling (BIM) tools, including a growth algorithm that employs digital means to grow the internal steel structure.

facts.fact: The calligraphy on the facade is by Emirati artist Matar Bin Lahej.
facts.quote: The phrases written on the outside of the museum are three quotes from Sheikh Mohammed: "We won't live for hundreds of years, but the products of our creativity can leave a legacy long after we are gone." "The future will be for those who will be able to imagine, design and build it, the future does not wait, the future can be designed and built today." "The secret of the renewal of life, the development of civilization and the progress of humanity is in one word: innovation." The Arabic calligraphy engraved quotes on the Museum of the Future in Dubai is written by Emirati artist Matar Bin Lahej.

facts.fact: In February 2023 the building achieved LEED Platinum certification.
facts.quote: On 3 February 2023, the building attained the LEED Platinum certification in terms of its green rating.

facts.fact: Farrells won an international competition to design the new Peak Tower, which opened in 1997 and later appeared on Hong Kong's $20 banknotes.
facts.quote: It was set up when the firm won an international competition to design the new Peak Tower, which opened in 1997 and was later featured on Hong Kong's $20 banknotes.

facts.fact: Terry Farrell designed the Peak Tower after setting up his practice in Hong Kong in 1990.
facts.quote: Subsequent to his setting up his practice in Hong Kong in 1990, he designed the Peak Tower, Kowloon Station development and the British Consulate-General, Hong Kong.

facts.fact: The Red Banner Textile Factory at Pionerskaya ulitsa 53, St Petersburg, was designed by Erich Mendelsohn and later partly redesigned by S. O. Ovsyannikov, E. A. Tretyakov and Hyppolit Pretreaus.
facts.quote: The Red Banner Textile Factory (Russian: Трикотажная фабрика «Красное Знамя»; Trikotazhnaya fabrika "Krasnoye Znamya") in St Petersburg, Pionerskaya ulitsa (Pioneers street), 53 was designed by Erich Mendelsohn and later partly redesigned by S. O. Ovsyannikov, E. A. Tretyakov, and Hyppolit Pretreaus (the senior architect of the project).

facts.fact: It was built between 1926 and 1937.
facts.quote: Built in 1926–1937.

facts.fact: In 1925 Mendelsohn became the first foreign architect asked to design in the USSR, on the strength of his dynamic Expressionist architecture.
facts.quote: Mendelsohn was the first foreign architect in 1925 to be asked to design in the USSR, on the basis of his dynamic, futuristic Expressionist architecture.

facts.fact: A model was made of a large factory, similar to but more functionalist than his earlier Luckenwalde hat factory.
facts.quote: A model was made of a large factory, similar though more functionalist in appearance to his earlier Luckenwalde hat factory.

facts.fact: The basic construction methods of the time could not realise the structure in full, so liberties were taken with Mendelsohn's design.
facts.quote: However, the primitive construction techniques of the time were insufficient to realise the structure in full, and liberties were taken with Mendelsohn's design.

facts.fact: Mendelsohn drew the first plan and designed the factory's power station, built in 1926 and officially recognised as Russian cultural heritage.
facts.quote: He drew an initial (later modified) plan of the factory and designed the power station of the factory, officially recognized as an object of Russian historical and cultural heritage (built in 1926).

facts.fact: Mendelsohn disowned the building after 1926, though he often used the model to show his approach to industrial architecture.
facts.quote: Mendelsohn disowned the building after its completion in 1926, although he would frequently make use of the model as an example of his approach to industrial architecture.

facts.fact: After a change of ownership, the exterior had been restored by early 2018.
facts.quote: With a change of ownership, by early 2018 the exterior had been restored.

facts.fact: Shakespeare's Globe is a reconstruction of the Globe Theatre, the Elizabethan playhouse of 1599 for which Shakespeare wrote his plays.
facts.quote: Shakespeare's Globe is a reconstruction of the Globe Theatre, an Elizabethan playhouse first built in 1599 for which William Shakespeare wrote his plays.

facts.fact: It was founded by actor and director Sam Wanamaker and built about 230 metres from the original site, in the historic open-air style.
facts.quote: The modern Shakespeare's Globe was founded by the actor and director Sam Wanamaker, and built about 230 metres (750 ft) from the site of the original theatre in the historic open-air style.

facts.fact: The design team was architect Theo Crosby of Pentagram, engineer Buro Happold and quantity surveyors Boyden & Co.
facts.quote: The design team consisted of architect Theo Crosby of Pentagram, structural and services engineer Buro Happold, and quantity surveyors from Boyden & Co.

facts.fact: The design was based on the research of historical adviser John Orrell.
facts.quote: A new Globe theatre was eventually built according to a design based on the research of historical adviser John Orrell.

facts.fact: Like the original, it has a thrust stage projecting into a large circular yard surrounded by three tiers of raked seating.
facts.quote: Like the original Globe, the modern theatre has a thrust stage that projects into a large circular yard surrounded by three tiers of raked seating.

facts.fact: It is built entirely of English oak with mortise and tenon joints, with no structural steel.
facts.quote: The building itself is constructed entirely of English oak, with mortise and tenon joints and is, in this sense, an "authentic" 16th-century timber-framed building as no structural steel was used.

facts.fact: It has what is claimed to be the first thatched roof allowed in London since the Great Fire of 1666.
facts.quote: The seats are simple benches (though cushions can be hired for performances) and the Globe has what has been claimed to be the first and only thatched roof permitted in London since the Great Fire of London in 1666.

facts.fact: The reconstruction was completed in 1997, and Queen Elizabeth II attended its official opening.
facts.quote: The reconstruction was completed in 1997 and the theatre's official opening was attended by Queen Elizabeth II.

facts.fact: The Museum of Modern Art in Warsaw (MSN) is a modern and contemporary art museum in Warsaw, Poland.
facts.quote: The Museum of Modern Art in Warsaw (Polish: Muzeum Sztuki Nowoczesnej w Warszawie, MSN), also known as MSN Warsaw, is a modern and contemporary art museum in Warsaw, Poland.

facts.fact: Its purpose-built home was designed by the New York studio Thomas Phifer and Partners, chosen in a two-stage tender in 2013–14.
facts.quote: The new custom-built museum was designed by the New York City-based architecture studio Thomas Phifer and Partners, chosen in the two-stage tender proceeding in 2013–14.

facts.fact: The building stands on the northern side of Plac Defilad, next to the Palace of Culture and Science.
facts.quote: Phifer designed the new Museum of Modern Art in Warsaw, located on the northern side of Plac Defilad next to the Palace of Culture and Science.

facts.fact: It opened on 25 October 2024.
facts.quote: Located on the northern side of Plac Defilad (city center), it was opened on 25 October 2024.

facts.fact: An earlier international competition was won in February 2007 by architect Christian Kerez, from over 100 designs.
facts.quote: The competition was won in February 2007 by architect C. Kerez. It was chosen from over 100 designs.

facts.fact: In May 2012 the city ended its contract with Christian Kerez.
facts.quote: Eventually however, in May 2012, the City terminated the contract with Christian Kerez.

facts.fact: The museum's director has described the new building as an iconic landmark in central Warsaw that reflects many aspects of Polish history.
facts.quote: In an interview with ARTnews on September 29 2025, the museum director Joanna Mytkowska highlighted that the new building is already an iconic architectural landmark in the centre of Warsaw, reflecting multiple aspects of Polish history including war time destruction, communism era and the post communism transformation period.

facts.fact: Wales Millennium Centre is Wales's national arts centre, in the Cardiff Bay area of Cardiff.
facts.quote: Wales Millennium Centre (Welsh: Canolfan Mileniwm Cymru) is Wales's national arts centre located in the Cardiff Bay area of Cardiff, Wales.

facts.fact: It was designed by Jonathan Adams of the local practice Percy Thomas Architects, with Arup Acoustics as acoustic designer and building engineer.
facts.quote: Wales Millennium Centre was designed by Jonathan Adams of local practice Percy Thomas Architects (taken over by Capita Group in 2004), with Arup Acoustics as the acoustic designer and building engineer.

facts.fact: Phase 1 opened in November 2004 and phase 2 in January 2009.
facts.quote: Phase 1 of the building was opened during the weekend of 26–28 November 2004 and phase 2 opened on 22 January 2009 with an inaugural concert.

facts.fact: The architect wanted a building that expressed "Welshness", using the Welsh materials that run through the country's history: slate, metal, wood and glass.
facts.quote: The architect's concept was a building that expressed "Welshness" and was instantly recognisable. The building was designed to reflect many different parts of Wales with local Welsh materials that dominate its history: slate, metal, wood and glass.

facts.fact: The outside is clad in multicoloured slate from Welsh quarries, with narrow windows set into the layers to suggest rock strata in sea cliffs.
facts.quote: The exterior of the building is clad in multi-coloured slate collected from Welsh quarries. Narrow windows are built into the layers of slate to give the impression of rock strata in sea cliffs.

facts.fact: Its main feature, the bronze-coloured dome over the Donald Gordon Theatre, is clad in stainless steel.
facts.quote: Wales Millennium Centre's main feature, the bronze coloured dome which covers the Donald Gordon Theatre, is clad in stainless steel.

facts.fact: Two lines by poet Gwyneth Lewis, in Welsh and English, are inscribed on the dome above the entrance, the letters formed by windows that glow at night.
facts.quote: Inscribed on the front of the dome, above the main entrance are two lines written by Welsh poet Gwyneth Lewis in Welsh and English. The lettering is formed by windows in the upstairs bar areas and is internally illuminated at night.

facts.fact: The main theatre, the Donald Gordon Theatre, has 1,896 seats.
facts.quote: The main theatre, the Donald Gordon Theatre, has 1,896 seats, and claims to be the second-largest stage in Europe.

facts.fact: The Musée Hergé in Louvain-la-Neuve, Belgium, is dedicated to the life and work of Hergé, creator of The Adventures of Tintin.
facts.quote: The Musée Hergé, or Hergé Museum, is a museum in Louvain-la-Neuve, Belgium, dedicated to the life and work of the cartoonist Georges Remi, who wrote under the pen name Hergé, creator of the series of comic albums The Adventures of Tintin, Quick & Flupke and The Adventures of Jo, Zette and Jocko.

facts.fact: It stands in the centre of Louvain-la-Neuve, on the edge of the green Parc de la Source.
facts.quote: The museum is located in the centre of Louvain-la-Neuve, on the edge of a green park, Le Parc de la Source.

facts.fact: The futuristic building was designed by Pritzker Prize-winning French architect Christian de Portzamparc, with interiors by cartoonist Joost Swarte.
facts.quote: The futuristic building was designed by the Pritzker Prize-winning French architect Christian de Portzamparc, with interiors designed by the cartoonist Joost Swarte.

facts.fact: The first stone was laid on 22 May 2007, the centenary of Hergé's birth, and the museum opened in June 2009.
facts.quote: On 22 May 2007 (the centenary of Hergé's birth), the first stone of the museum was laid. Two years later, in June 2009, the museum opened its doors to the public.

facts.fact: It has three floors with nine exhibition rooms, a café, a shop and a small cinema.
facts.quote: It consists of three floors with a total of nine exhibition rooms, a café, museum shop and mini cinema.

facts.fact: Visitors begin their visit on the top floor.
facts.quote: Visitors begin at the top floor.

facts.fact: A long walkway looks over the lobby on one side and an oak forest outside on the other.
facts.quote: Visitors then cross a long walkway, viewing the lobby on one side and an oak forest outside on the other.

facts.fact: Its address, Rue Labrador 26, is Tintin's first home in the books.
facts.quote: Its address is "Rue Labrador 26", Tintin's first home in the books.

facts.fact: The Grand Théâtre de Québec is a performing arts complex in Quebec City, Canada.
facts.quote: The Grand Théâtre de Québec (French pronunciation: [ɡʁɑ̃ teɑtʁ də kebɛk]) is a performing arts complex in Quebec City, Quebec, Canada.

facts.fact: It was conceived to mark the Canadian Centennial of 1967 and the 1864 Quebec Conference, a key step towards Confederation.
facts.quote: It was conceived to commemorate the Canadian Centennial of 1967 and the Quebec Conference, 1864, one of the key meetings leading to the Canadian Confederation of 1867.

facts.fact: Victor Prus's design was chosen from several entries in a national competition in 1964.
facts.quote: He designed several major buildings in Quebec which won many prizes, such as the Grand Théâtre de Québec in Quebec City; his designs were chosen from those of several entries in a national competition in 1964.

facts.fact: Construction resumed in late 1967 after a halt, and the theatre officially opened on 16 January 1971.
facts.quote: Construction resumed in late 1967 but the theatre was not officially opened until January 16, 1971.

facts.fact: Its larger hall, the Salle Louis-Fréchette, has 1,885 seats.
facts.quote: The theatre has two venues: Salle Louis Fréchette, with 1,885 seats, is named after the 19th-century French-Canadian writer Louis-Honoré Fréchette.

facts.fact: In 1969 the Catalan artist Jordi Bonet was commissioned to decorate the lobby with a mural.
facts.quote: In 1969, Jordi Bonet, a Catalan artist resident in Quebec, was commissioned to decorate the theatre's lobby with a mural.

facts.fact: In 2020 the building was restored and wrapped in a glass envelope on a steel frame, designed by Lemay and Atelier 21, to protect its architecture and Bonet's mural set into the facade.
facts.quote: In 2020, the Grand Théâtre de Québec was restored and covered with a glass envelope supported by a steel frame, designed by Lemay and Atelier 21, to preserve the structure's architecture and a sculptural mural from artist Jordi Bonet embedded into the façade.

facts.fact: In 2021 it received the RAIC Innovation in Architecture Award, in part for innovations honouring the original Victor Prus building.
facts.quote: In 2021 Grand Théâtre de Québec received the Canadian RAIC: Royal Architectural Institute of Canada "Innovation in Architecture Award" in part for "a host of notable innovations in the spirit of honouring the original Victor Prus building".

facts.fact: The Israel Goldstein Synagogue is a synagogue on the Edmond J. Safra Givat Ram campus of the Hebrew University of Jerusalem.
facts.quote: The Rabbi Dr. I. Goldstein Synagogue, also known as the Israel Goldstein Synagogue, is a Jewish congregation and synagogue, located on the Edmond J. Safra Givat Ram campus of the Hebrew University of Jerusalem.

facts.fact: It was designed in an organic style by Israeli architects Heinz Rau and David Resnick, called a landmark of local architecture, and won the Rechter Prize in 1964.
facts.quote: Designed in the organic style by two Israeli architects, the German-born Heinrich Heinz Rau and the Brazilian-born David Resnick, the synagogue building was listed as one of the "ten most beautiful synagogues in Israel," and called "without a doubt, a landmark in local architecture." In 1964, the synagogue design was awarded the Rechter Prize by the Israeli Architects Association.

facts.fact: The synagogue was consecrated on 7 August 1957.
facts.quote: The synagogue was consecrated on August 7, 1957.

facts.fact: When it was built in 1957, the new Givat Ram campus was largely undeveloped.
facts.quote: Givat Ram, the site of the new campus, was largely undeveloped in 1957 when the synagogue was built.

facts.fact: It is 3.73 metres high, with an exterior shaped as a concrete hemisphere resting on eight arches.
facts.quote: The synagogue is 3.73 m (12.25 ft) high, with an exterior in the shape of a "concrete hemisphere" on eight arches.

facts.fact: The floor is a raised platform and the interior has no windows, lit by light rippling up from below; the domed space holds 100 worshippers.
facts.quote: The floor of the synagogue is a raised platform, and the interior has no windows, "yet in a sense is adorned by light, which ripples up from below on all sides." Within the domed worship space there is room for 100 worshippers.

facts.fact: In 1975 it appeared on an Israeli postage stamp series on "Architecture in Israel".
facts.quote: In 1975 the synagogue was featured in a series of Israeli postage stamps dedicated to "Architecture in Israel."

facts.fact: The Matenadaran, officially the Mesrop Mashtots Institute of Ancient Manuscripts, is the largest centre for keeping and studying Armenian manuscripts, combining museum, archive and research institute.
facts.quote: The Matenadaran (Armenian: Մատենադարան), officially the Mesrop Mashtots Institute of Ancient Manuscripts, is the largest center for the storage, study and popularization of Armenian manuscripts, combining the functions of a museum, archive and scientific institution.

facts.fact: Yerevan's chief architect Mark Grigorian was commissioned to design it in October 1939.
facts.quote: Yerevan's chief architect Mark Grigorian was commissioned by the Soviet Armenian authorities to design it in October 1939, almost immediately after the manuscripts were decided to be transferred to Yerevan.

facts.fact: It was built from 1945 to 1957–58, with a pause from 1947 to 1953, and its interiors were finished between 1957 and 1959.
facts.quote: Its construction lasted from 1945 to 1957–58, with a pause from 1947 to 1953 due to a shortage of skilled laborers. Interior finishing was completed between 1957 and 1959.

facts.fact: It sits on a slope at the north-eastern end of Mashtots Avenue, rising 18 metres above the street and closing the view along the avenue.
facts.quote: The Matenadaran building is situated on a slope at the northeastern end of Mashtots Avenue, the main thoroughfare in central Yerevan. Rising 18 m (59 ft) above street level, it forms a visual endpoint for the avenue and serves as an intermediate link in the spatial composition that includes the statue of Mother Armenia and its large pedestal atop the hill.

facts.fact: Standing 22.4 metres tall, it is a simple cube faced with local grey basalt, with a facade and interior influenced by medieval Armenian architecture.
facts.quote: Standing 22.4 m (73 ft) tall, it is a simple cube faced with local gray basalt. The design of its façade and interior are influenced by medieval Armenian architecture.

facts.fact: The arched central entrance flanked by tall narrow niches is inspired by the 12th-century gavit of the Church of the Holy Apostles at Ani.
facts.quote: Grigorian believed that the "attractive features of national architecture should be expressed in this building as vividly and strongly as possible." Its rectangular façade—a tall arched central entrance flanked by two tall and narrow decorative niches on both sides—is specifically inspired by the eastern façade of the 12th century southern gavit (narthex) of the Church of the Holy Apostles (Arakelots) of Ani, the grand capital of Bagratid Armenia.

facts.fact: The interior is inspired by medieval Armenian gavits of the 11th and 12th centuries.
facts.quote: Its interior was likewise inspired by medieval Armenian architecture, especially eleventh and twelfth century gavits (zhamatuns).

facts.fact: A new building by Arthur Meschian was later added to hold the growing collection.
facts.quote: The new building of the Matenadaran was designed by Arthur Meschian, an architect better known as a musician, to accommodate the growing collection of manuscripts.

facts.fact: The Four Seasons Centre for the Performing Arts is a 2,071-seat theatre at University Avenue and Queen Street West in Toronto, across from Osgoode Hall.
facts.quote: The Four Seasons Centre for the Performing Arts is a 2,071-seat theatre in Toronto, Ontario, Canada, located at the southeast corner of University Avenue and Queen Street West, across from Osgoode Hall.

facts.fact: It is the home of the Canadian Opera Company and the National Ballet of Canada.
facts.quote: It is the home of the Canadian Opera Company (COC) and the National Ballet of Canada.

facts.fact: Ten firms submitted proposals, and the modernist design by Diamond Schmitt Architects, led by Jack Diamond, was chosen.
facts.quote: Ten architectural firms submitted proposals, and the modernist design by Canadian company Diamond Schmitt Architects, headed by Jack Diamond, was selected.

facts.fact: It opened on 14 June 2006 with a gala concert.
facts.quote: The centre had its grand opening on 14 June 2006 with a gala concert.

facts.fact: The five-tier, horseshoe-shaped auditorium was modelled on European opera houses, especially the National Theatre Munich.
facts.quote: The five-tiered, horseshoe-shaped auditorium was modelled after European opera houses and, specifically, on the dimensions and configuration of the National Theatre Munich with which Richard Bradshaw was well acquainted.

facts.fact: To shut out traffic, subway and streetcar rumble, the theatre sits on 489 rubber insulating pads.
facts.quote: To prevent audience members from detecting specific sounds and vibrations including traffic noise, the rumble from the adjacent Line 1 Yonge–University subway line and 501 Queen streetcar line, and even the sirens of the emergency vehicles rushing to the nearby hospitals, the theatre sits on 489 rubber insulating pads.

facts.fact: The glass walls of the City Room foyer face University Avenue and Queen Street, while the east, south and north sides are clad in dark brick.
facts.quote: The City Room glass walls, curtain walls held by steel fixtures, look out on University Ave and Queen Street. The east, south and north sides are clad in dark brick.

facts.fact: Diamond defended the plain exterior: "You do not make a city out of iconic pieces."
facts.quote: Architect Diamond defended his rather plain design, stating, "You do not make a city out of iconic pieces." Two exterior features were omitted to reduce costs.

facts.fact: The interior includes an unusual glass staircase.
facts.quote: It was completed in 2006, and the interior design includes an unusual glass staircase.

facts.fact: The José Martí Memorial honours Cuba's national hero José Martí, on the north side of the Plaza de la Revolución in Havana's Vedado area.
facts.quote: The José Martí Memorial (Spanish: Monumento a José Martí) is a memorial to José Martí, a national hero of Cuba, located on the northern side of the Plaza de la Revolución in the Vedado area of Havana.

facts.fact: It consists of a star-shaped tower, a statue of Martí surrounded by six columns, and gardens.
facts.quote: It consists of a star-shaped tower, a statue of Martí surrounded by six columns, and gardens.

facts.fact: The 109-metre tower, designed by Jean Labatut under architect Raoul Otero de Galarraga, is a five-pointed star in plan, clad in grey Cuban marble from the Isla de Pinos.
facts.quote: The 109 m (358 ft) tower, designed by Jean Labatut under architect Raoul Otero de Galarraga, is in the form of a five-pointed star, encased in grey Cuban marble from the Isla de Pinos.

facts.fact: Batista chose the third-placed competition design by a team led by Raoul Otero de Galarraga that included Enrique Luis Varela, his Minister of Works, and Princeton professor Jean Labatut.
facts.quote: Eager to garner popular support after seizing power, Batista committed to pushing ahead with the construction of a monument to Martí; but rather than proceeding with the competition winner, he selected the design that had come third in the competition, created by a group of architects headed by Raoul Otero de Galarraga, a 1905 graduate of Harvard University, and included Enrique Luis Varela, Batista's Minister of Works and his personal friend, and Princeton University Professor Jean Labatut.

facts.fact: Construction of the tower began in 1953, the 100th anniversary of Martí's birth.
facts.quote: Construction of the tower began in 1953 on the 100th anniversary of José Martí's birth.

facts.fact: The monument was completed in 1958, in the last days of the Batista dictatorship.
facts.quote: The Chapel was finally demolished and the monument was completed in 1958 during the final days of the Batista dictatorship.

facts.fact: An enclosed observation deck on the top floor, the highest point in Havana, is reached by lift.
facts.quote: The selected design includes an enclosed observation deck on the top floor, the highest point in Havana, accessible by elevator which gives commanding views over the city in all directions.

facts.fact: Outside stands an 18-metre white marble statue of Martí carved on site by Juan José Sicre.
facts.quote: Outside, facing over the plaza and towards the mural of Che Guevara on the Ministry of the Interior on the opposite side of the square, is an 18 m (59 ft) white marble statue of Martí carved in situ by Sicre and surrounded by six half-height marble columns.

facts.fact: Pointe-à-Callière is a museum of archaeology and history in Old Montreal.
facts.quote: Pointe-à-Callière Museum (French: Musée Pointe-à-Callière, pronounced [myze pwɛ̃t a kaljɛʁ]) is a museum of archaeology and history in Old Montreal, Quebec, Canada.

facts.fact: It was founded in 1992 as part of the celebrations of Montreal's 350th birthday.
facts.quote: It was founded in 1992 as part of celebrations to mark Montreal's 350th birthday.

facts.fact: The Pointe-à-Callière Museum is among the main works of Montreal architect Dan Hanganu.
facts.quote: His project highlights include the Pointe-à-Callière Museum, the Théâtre du Nouveau Monde, the Saint-Benoît-du-Lac Church, the UQAM Design Pavilion, the Cirque du Soleil studio, HEC Montréal, the Centre des arts Juliette-Lassonde, Hotel Godin, the Montréal Archival Centre, the Nahum Gelber Law Library of McGill University, l’Anglicane de Lévis, the Rimouski Arts Centre, and residential areas in Val de l’Anse.

facts.fact: Its main entrance building, L'Éperon, rises over the point of land where French settlers including Maisonneuve and Jeanne Mance landed in 1642.
facts.quote: The main entrance of the museum, the L'Éperon building, rises above the point of land where Paul de Chomedey, Sieur de Maisonneuve, Jeanne Mance and other French settlers landed in 1642.

facts.fact: The museum was built on piles so that the archaeological finds below were left undisturbed and protected.
facts.quote: The museum was constructed on pilings to preserve existing finds undisturbed and protected.

facts.fact: Some of the remains uncovered during construction were left in place as part of the permanent display.
facts.quote: Some of the archaeological remains exposed during construction of the building has been left in situ as part of the museum's permanent display on the history of the city.

facts.fact: The main building's site was once occupied by the Royal Insurance Building, Montreal's second Customs House from 1871 to 1917.
facts.quote: The site of Pointe-à-Callière Museum main building site was once occupied by the Royal Insurance Building, which was also Montreal’s second Customs House from 1871 to 1917.

facts.fact: It has received more than fifty national and international awards, including awards for architecture.
facts.quote: It has received more than fifty national and international awards, including those in museography, architecture, and for cultural, educational and community activities.

facts.fact: St Paul's Cathedral in Abidjan was designed by Italian architect Aldo Spirito and is the mother church of the Archdiocese of Abidjan.
facts.quote: The cathedral, which was designed by the Italian architect Aldo Spirito, serves as the mother church for the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Abidjan.

facts.fact: Pope John Paul II consecrated its first stone on 11 May 1980.
facts.quote: The first stone of the cathedral was consecrated on May 11, 1980, by Pope John Paul II during his first pastoral visit to Côte d'Ivoire.

facts.fact: The pope formally consecrated the cathedral on his second visit to Abidjan in August 1985.
facts.quote: The cathedral was formally consecrated by the pope during his second visit to Abidjan in August 1985.

facts.fact: Its most striking external feature is a tall concrete structure shaped like an anthropomorphic giant.
facts.quote: The striking external feature of the cathedral (which attracts visitors at the entrance itself) is the tall concrete structure, which is shaped like an anthropomorphic giant.

facts.fact: The winged cross is held by seven cables anchored to the triangular main building, so it seems to be pulled towards the lagoon.
facts.quote: The structure of the Cross, which is winged on both flanks, is held in position through seven cables which are anchored to the main building of the cathedral which is in a triangular shape; it creates an elevated vision that the structure is being tugged towards the lagoon.

facts.fact: It is built of concrete, steel, travertine, stone and stained glass.
facts.quote: The materials used for building this unique edifice consists of concrete, steel, travertine (a form of limestone deposited by mineral springs), stones and sheets of stained glasses.

facts.fact: It stands on a hillock with commanding views over Abidjan and the Bay of Cocody.
facts.quote: It is dominantly located on a hillock providing commanding views of the city of Abidjan, and overlooking the Bay of Cocody.

facts.fact: It holds 5,000 people, with seats for 3,500.
facts.quote: It can accommodate 5,000 devotees, with seating for 3,500, with the remainder being standing space.

facts.fact: The Old Parliament House in New Delhi, formerly the Council House, was the seat of India's Parliament from 26 January 1950 to 18 September 2023.
facts.quote: The Old Parliament House, officially known as the Samvidhan Sadan (Constitution House) and formerly known as the Council House, was the seat of the Parliament of India between 26 January 1950 and 18 September 2023.

facts.fact: It was designed by British architects Edwin Lutyens and Herbert Baker and built between 1921 and 1927.
facts.quote: The building was designed by British architects Edwin Lutyens and Herbert Baker and was constructed between 1921 and 1927.

facts.fact: Lutyens proposed a circular plan, which he thought most efficient for the triangular plot.
facts.quote: Lutyens proposed a circular design for the new building, which he believed would be the most efficient given the triangular shape of the plot of land on which the building is located.

facts.fact: Its style mixes Greek and Roman classical architecture with structural elements and decorative motifs from Indian architecture.
facts.quote: The architectural style of the structure is an amalgamation of classical architecture, inspired from Greece and Rome, alongside structural elements and decorative motifs from Indian architecture.

facts.fact: The exterior has 144 sandstone columns.
facts.quote: The building consisted of 144 sandstone columns on the exterior.

facts.fact: A circular central chamber at its core was surrounded by three semicircular halls for the Chamber of Princes, the Council of State and the Central Legislative Assembly.
facts.quote: At the core was the circular central chamber, and which was surrounded by three semicircular halls, for the sessions of the Chamber of Princes, the Council of State, and the Central Legislative Assembly.

facts.fact: It was surrounded by large gardens, with a perimeter of latticed sandstone jali railings.
facts.quote: The structure was surrounded by expansive gardens, and its perimeter enclosed by jali (latticed sandstone railings).

facts.fact: A new Parliament House built next to it was inaugurated on 28 May 2023, replacing the old building.
facts.quote: A new Parliament House built adjacent to this building was inaugurated on 28 May 2023, replacing the old Parliament building.

facts.fact: The Ontario Science Centre, originally the Centennial Centre of Science and Technology, is a science museum in Toronto.
facts.quote: The Ontario Science Centre, originally the Centennial Centre of Science and Technology, is a science museum and educational organization temporarily located at Harbourfront Centre in Toronto, Canada.

facts.fact: Toronto architect Raymond Moriyama was hired to design the site.
facts.quote: Toronto architect Raymond Moriyama was hired to design the site.

facts.fact: It was Moriyama's first large project as an independent architect.
facts.quote: The Ontario Science Centre was Moriyama's first large-scale project as an independent architect.

facts.fact: It missed the 1967 Centennial and opened to the public on 26 September 1969.
facts.quote: However, construction was not completed by 1967, and the Science Centre did not open to the public until two years later, on 26 September 1969.

facts.fact: Built into the side of a ravine of the Don River, it was a series of buildings at different levels on a steep hill, joined by escalators, with large windows onto the forest and river.
facts.quote: Built into the side of a ravine formed by a branch of the Don River, the museum consisted of a series of buildings constructed at different levels on a steep hill and connected by escalators. Large windows provided views of the surrounding forest and river.

facts.fact: The original buildings, designed in the early 1960s, are in the Brutalist style.
facts.quote: Designed in the early 1960s, the original buildings were built in the Brutalist architectural style.

facts.fact: The glass front entrance had a large exposed steel-cable structure.
facts.quote: The glass facade of the front entrance had a large, exposed steel cable structure.

facts.fact: The Ontario government closed the Don Mills building in June 2024 after an engineering report found a high risk of roof collapse.
facts.quote: It was closed by the Government of Ontario in June 2024 after an engineering report identified a high risk of roof collapse.

facts.fact: The Union Buildings are the official seat of the South African government and house the offices of the President.
facts.quote: The Union Buildings (Afrikaans: Uniegebou) form the official seat of the South African Government and also house the offices of the President of South Africa.

facts.fact: They stand on the highest point of Pretoria and are a South African national heritage site.
facts.quote: Though not in the centre of Pretoria, the Union Buildings occupy the highest point of Pretoria, and constitute a South African national heritage site.

facts.fact: Built of light sandstone, they were designed by Sir Herbert Baker in the English monumental style and are 285 metres long.
facts.quote: These buildings, built from light sandstone, were designed by the architect Sir Herbert Baker in the English monumental style and are 285 m long.

facts.fact: A semicircular colonnade in the middle joins two side wings, representing the union of a formerly divided people.
facts.quote: They have a semi-circular colonnade at the middle, and the two wings at the sides, this serves to represent the union of a formerly divided people.

facts.fact: The site was a disused quarry, and its excavations were used to create the amphitheatre.
facts.quote: The site was that of a disused quarry and the existing excavations were used to create the amphitheatre, which was set about with ornamental pools, fountains, sculptures, balustrades, and trees.

facts.fact: Baker strongly favoured the Meintjieskop hill, which reminded him of the acropolises of Greece and Asia Minor.
facts.quote: However, Herbert Baker was strongly in favour of Meintjieskop, which was within 1.6 kilometres of the centre of Pretoria and reminded him strongly of some of the acropolises of Greece and Asia Minor, where he had studied Mediterranean architecture.

facts.fact: Baker used local materials where possible: granite was quarried on site and Buiskop sandstone used for the courtyards.
facts.quote: Baker used indigenous materials as far as possible. The granite was quarried on site while Buiskop sandstone was used for the courtyards.

facts.fact: About 1,265 workers took three years to build it, finishing in 1913.
facts.quote: Taking 1,265 workers over three years to build, the structure was completed in 1913 at a total cost of £1,310,640 for the building and £350,000 for the site.

facts.fact: Villa Isola, now Bumi Siliwangi, is an Art Deco building in the north of Bandung, Indonesia.
facts.quote: Villa Isola (now Bumi Siliwangi) is an art-deco building in the northern part of Bandung, the capital of West Java province of Indonesia.

facts.fact: Overlooking a valley with views of the city, it was completed in 1933 by Dutch architect Wolff Schoemaker for the media tycoon Dominique Willem Berretty.
facts.quote: Overlooking the valley with the view of the city, Villa Isola was completed in 1933 by the Dutch architect Wolff Schoemaker for the Dutch media tycoon Dominique Willem Berretty, the founder of the Aneta press-agency in the Dutch East Indies.

facts.fact: Built as Berretty's private house, it later became a hotel and now houses the rectorate of the Indonesia University of Education.
facts.quote: The original purpose of the building was for Berretty's private house, but then it was transformed into a hotel after his death and now it serves as the rectorate building of Indonesia University of Education.

facts.fact: Schoemaker's design was influenced by Javanese philosophy: the building lies on a north–south axis, facing Mount Tangkuban Perahu to the north and Bandung to the south.
facts.quote: The design of the Villa Isola by the architect Wolff Schoemaker, was influenced by indigenous Javanese philosophy. The orientation of the building is according to the north—south axis, where the building faces Mount Tangkuban Perahu to the north and the city of Bandung to the south.

facts.fact: Schoemaker mixed the Art Deco style with local ornament.
facts.quote: Schoemaker was a firm follower of the art-deco style, which he mixed with local ornaments.

facts.fact: The circle is the main theme of the complex, inside and out, including the gardens.
facts.quote: Circle is the main theme of the complex, both inside and outside the villa, including the gardens.

facts.fact: The west and east corridors also act as air channels, regulating the building's temperature in the tropical climate.
facts.quote: Besides as connecting halls to the terraces, the west and east corridors function as "pipelines" to regulate air in the building, isolating the thermal condition of the tropical climate.

facts.fact: It has a steel frame, with concrete filling the skeleton and the floors.
facts.quote: The foundation was built of steel and concrete was used to fill the skeleton and the floors between iron bars.

facts.fact: The Royal Exhibition Building is a UNESCO World Heritage-listed building in Melbourne, built in 1879–1880 as part of the international exhibition movement.
facts.quote: The Royal Exhibition Building is a UNESCO World Heritage-listed building in Melbourne, Victoria, Australia, built in 1879–1880 as part of the international exhibition movement, which presented over 50 exhibitions between 1851 and 1915 around the globe.

facts.fact: Eighteen designs were entered in the competition, won by local architect Joseph Reed.
facts.quote: Eighteen entries were made with the winner, celebrated local architect Joseph Reed, receiving first prize of £300.

facts.fact: Built of brick, timber, steel and slate, it draws on Byzantine, Romanesque, Lombardic and Italian Renaissance styles.
facts.quote: Composed of brick, timber, steel, and slate, the Exhibition Building is representative of the Byzantine, Romanesque, Lombardic and Italian Renaissance styles.

facts.fact: Its dome was modelled on Florence Cathedral.
facts.quote: The dome was modeled on the Florence Cathedral, while the main pavilions were influenced by the style of Rundbogenstil and several buildings from Normandy, Caen and Paris.

facts.fact: It has a Latin-cross plan, with long nave-like wings running east–west from the central dome and a shorter wing to the north.
facts.quote: The building has the scale of the French Beaux Arts, with a cruciform plan in the shape of a Latin cross, with long nave-like wings symmetrically placed east–west about the central dome, and a shorter wing to the north.

facts.fact: Windows in the drum of the dome were designed to bring sunlight into the crossing.
facts.quote: At the crossing, windows in the drum of the dome were designed to bring in sunlight for a bright open space.

facts.fact: The foundation stone was laid on 19 February 1879 and the building was completed in just 18 months, opening on 1 October 1880.
facts.quote: The foundation stone was laid by Victorian governor George Bowen on 19 February 1879 and it was completed in just 18 months, opening on 1 October 1880, as the Melbourne International Exhibition.

facts.fact: The first Parliament of Australia opened here on 9 May 1901.
facts.quote: The most significant event to occur in the Exhibition Building was the opening of the first Parliament of Australia on 9 May 1901, following the inauguration of the Commonwealth of Australia on 1 January.

facts.fact: In 2004 it became the first building in Australia to gain UNESCO World Heritage status.
facts.quote: It received restoration throughout the 1990s and in 2004 became the first building in Australia to be awarded UNESCO World Heritage status, being one of the last remaining major 19th-century exhibition buildings in the world.

facts.fact: The Casablanca Cathedral, or Church of the Sacred Heart, is a former church west of the Arab League Park in Casablanca, Morocco.
facts.quote: The Casablanca Cathedral (Arabic: كاتدرائية الدار البيضاء, French: Cathédrale de Casablanca), or Church of the Sacred Heart (Arabic: كنيسة القلب المقدس, French: Église du Sacré-Cœur), is a former church located west of the Arab League Park in Casablanca, Morocco.

facts.fact: It was built in 1930.
facts.quote: The Casablanca Cathedral was constructed in 1930.

facts.fact: It was designed by French architect Paul Tournon in the Art Deco style.
facts.quote: The church was designed by French architect Paul Tournon, in the Art Deco style.

facts.fact: Although called a cathedral, it was never the seat of a bishop.
facts.quote: It is commonly referred to as a cathedral, although in reality, it has never technically been one as it was never the seat of a bishop.

facts.fact: It stopped serving as a church in 1956, after Moroccan independence, and became a cultural centre open to visitors.
facts.quote: The former church ceased its religious function in 1956, after the independence of Morocco. It subsequently became a cultural centre which is open to visitors.

facts.fact: Established in 1854 as the Melbourne Public Library, it is Australia's oldest public library and one of the first free libraries in the world.
facts.quote: Located in Melbourne, it was established in 1854 as the Melbourne Public Library, making it Australia's oldest public library and one of the first free libraries in the world.

facts.fact: Joseph Reed won the design competition, and his firm and its successors designed most of the later extensions.
facts.quote: A competition was held, won by the recently arrived architect Joseph Reed, whose firm and its successors went on to design most of the later extensions, as well as numerous 19th-century landmarks such as the Melbourne Town Hall, and the Royal Exhibition Building.

facts.fact: The first stage, the centre of the Swanston Street wing, opened on 11 February 1856.
facts.quote: The library's first stage (the central part of the Swanston Street wing) opened on 11 February 1856, with a collection of 3,800 books chosen by Mr Justice Barry, the President of Trustees.

facts.fact: The complex was built in many stages and finally filled the whole city block in 1992.
facts.quote: The complex of buildings that now house the Library was built in numerous stages, housing various library spaces, art galleries and museum displays, finally filling the entire block in 1992.

facts.fact: The landmark Domed Reading Room opened in 1913, designed by Norman G. Peebles of Bates Smart.
facts.quote: The landmark Domed Reading Room was opened in 1913, and was designed by Norman G. Peebles of Bates Smart.

facts.fact: Its six-storey octagonal space was designed to hold over a million books and up to 600 readers.
facts.quote: Its six storey high octagonal space was designed to hold over a million books and up to 600 readers; as of 2024 it can house 32,000 books and 320 readers at its desks.

facts.fact: The dome is 34.75 metres in both diameter and height, with an oculus nearly 5 metres wide, and was the largest in the world when completed.
facts.quote: It is 34.75 metres in both diameter and height, and its oculus is nearly 5 metres wide. The dome was the largest in the world on completion.

facts.fact: The reading room reopened in 2003 as the La Trobe Reading Room, with the dome's skylights, covered by copper since 1959, revealed again.
facts.quote: The reading room was refurbished and reopened in 2003 as the La Trobe Reading Room, with the dome's skylights that had been hidden behind copper sheathing since 1959 again revealed.

facts.fact: Fort Jesus, on Mombasa Island, was designed by Italian architect Giovanni Battista Cairati and built between 1593 and 1596 to guard the Old Port of Mombasa.
facts.quote: Designed by the Italian architect Giovanni Battista Cairati, it was built between 1593 and 1596 by order of King Felipe II of Spain, who also reigned as King Filipe I of Portugal and the Algarves, to guard the Old Port of Mombasa.

facts.fact: Cairati based the design on the ideas of Italian architect Pietro Cataneo, with Gaspar Rodrigues as master builder.
facts.quote: Cairati, inspired by Italian architect Pietro Cataneo, designed the fort, with the master builder being Gaspar Rodrigues.

facts.fact: The design is Renaissance, but the masonry techniques, materials and labour are thought to have come from local Swahili people.
facts.quote: Although the design of Fort Jesus is an example of Renaissance architecture, the masonry techniques, building materials, and labor are believed to have been provided by the local Swahili people.

facts.fact: Seen from the air the fort is shaped like a man; it is roughly square with four bulwarks at its corners, and is considered a masterpiece of late Renaissance military fortification.
facts.quote: The fort, built in the shape of a man viewed from the air, is roughly square with four bulwarks at its corners and is considered a masterpiece of late Renaissance military fortification.

facts.fact: It was the first European-style fort built outside Europe designed to resist cannon fire.
facts.quote: It was the first European-style fort constructed outside of Europe designed to resist cannon fire.

facts.fact: Its walls are 18 metres high: the original Portuguese fort was 15 metres, and the Omani Arabs added 3 metres.
facts.quote: The height of the walls is 18 meters. The original Portuguese fort had a height of 15 meters, but the Oman Arabs added 3 meters upon capturing the fort.

facts.fact: The fort combines Portuguese, Arab and British elements from the powers that held it.
facts.quote: The fort combines Portuguese, Arab, and British elements (these being the major powers that held it at different times in history).

facts.fact: It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2011, as one of the best-preserved 16th-century Portuguese military fortifications.
facts.quote: In 2011, it was declared a World Heritage Site by UNESCO and highlighted as one of the most outstanding and well-preserved examples of 16th-century Portuguese military fortifications.

facts.fact: The Old Government Buildings are a four-storey, 143-room wooden heritage complex on Lambton Quay in central Wellington.
facts.quote: The Old Government Buildings are a 4-storey, 143-room wooden heritage building complex located on the Government Buildings Historic Reserve, on Lambton Quay in central Pipitea, Wellington.

facts.fact: It is the largest timber-framed building in the Southern Hemisphere.
facts.quote: It is the largest timber-framed building in the Southern Hemisphere.

facts.fact: It was completed in 1876 on land reclaimed from Wellington Harbour to house New Zealand's government and public service.
facts.quote: The buildings were completed in 1876 on land reclaimed from Wellington Harbour to house the young New Zealand Government and its public service.

facts.fact: The architect was William Clayton and the contractors were Scoular and Archibald.
facts.quote: The architect was William Clayton and the contractors were Scoular and Archibald.

facts.fact: It was first planned in concrete and timber, but the cost of concrete led to building it in timber alone.
facts.quote: It was originally planned to have the building constructed in concrete and timber, but the cost of concrete at the time led to a decision to build in timber alone.

facts.fact: Its Italianate, Neo-Renaissance design mimics stone, made to look like an Italian stone palace to convey strength and stability.
facts.quote: The Italianate, Neo-Renaissance style was usually the domain of stone buildings, thus the building is designed to mimic stone. As an important symbol of nationhood, the building was constructed to resemble an Italian stone palace to help convey its strength and stability in the expanding empire.

facts.fact: The timber is native kauri.
facts.quote: The timber is native kauri, which could not be replicated because New Zealand's remaining public kauri forests are permanently protected.

facts.fact: It reopened in January 1996 after restoration, with Victoria University's Law Faculty as its new tenant.
facts.quote: The government buildings were formally reopened in January 1996 after the Law Faculty of Victoria University signed a 50-year tenancy that year and became its new occupants.

facts.fact: It is classified as a Category 1 historic building by Heritage New Zealand.
facts.quote: Classified as a Category 1 historic building by Heritage New Zealand, the Old Government Buildings are also a popular tourist destination.
